Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Stop rebuilding one clearance field per colony, and drop the heap for buckets

Equilibrium is the slowest generator in the catalog by a wide margin - 288 ms a map
against 174 for the next one, about 9 per cent of the whole catalog's generation time -
so it is where profiling starts. Sampling 400 maps at 256x256 with four colonies put
almost all of it in scoreShape, the shape pass's cost function, which runs once per
annealing proposal. Two things in it were waste, and neither changes a single map:
456 golden rows and all 17 contract suites are unchanged.

First, scoreShape asked widestWalkClearance for each colony's way out, and that
function begins by computing clearance(t, mask) - a full distance transform of the
land. The field depends on nothing but the mask, which is the same for every colony, so
a four-colony map built it four times a proposal and an eight-colony map eight times.
It was 30 per cent of the generator's run time. There is now an overload taking a
precomputed field, and the caller computes it once; clearance fell from 4614 samples to
1391. The old signature stays for the validators that ask a single question.

Second, what was left on top was the widest-path search's own priority queue, with two
fifths of its time inside __pop_heap. The keys are clearances - small bounded integers,
at most half the shorter side - so a comparison heap is the wrong structure. A bucket
per width walked from the widest down gives the same visit order at O(1) a push and a
pop, and touches a flat vector instead of sifting a growing array. It is correct for
the same reason Dijkstra is: relaxation only ever produces min(width, room), which
cannot exceed the bucket being drained, so the first pop of a tile is final.

Also lifts the three map-sized buffers scoreShape allocated on every proposal onto the
Shape scratch that already existed for the walk queue.

Generation time for Equilibrium, measured with the golden test's telemetry mode, mean
of three seeds at 256x256 with four colonies:

  before             297.8 ms
  clearance hoisted  239.2 ms   -19.7%
  bucket queue       210.7 ms   -29.3% overall

Wall clock for 20 maps end to end: 5.93 s to 4.82 s at 256x256 with four colonies, and
5.45 s to 4.20 s for three maps at 512x512 with eight colonies and Patient effort, where
there are eight redundant transforms a proposal rather than four.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Read the walk field once per cell, where aliasing stopped the compiler doing it

Two loops in Equilibrium's shape pass reload values the compiler is not allowed to
assume are stable, because in both cases the reads and the writes are through vectors
it cannot prove disjoint.

walkLand wrote steps[next] = steps[i] + 1 inside the neighbour loop, so steps[i] was
reloaded on each of the four steps even though it cannot change: a cell is written only
while still unvisited, and this one has been dequeued. The scoring loop was worse - it
indexed s.walk[k][i] four times a cell and accumulated straight into three vector
elements, so the step count and all three running totals went back to memory every
iteration.

Both now read into locals. No map moves: 456 golden rows and 17 contract suites
unchanged.

Equilibrium's generation time, mean of three seeds at 256x256 with four colonies:

  before this branch's profiling   297.8 ms
  clearance hoisted out of the loop 239.2 ms
  bucket queue for the widest walk  210.7 ms
  these two loops                   193.0 ms   -35.2% overall

Worth recording what is NOT the problem, so nobody looks again: cache. The search runs
on a 32x32 lattice, so a walk field is 4 KB, the whole per-proposal working set about
25 KB, and it sits in L1 throughout - shrinking the step counts to int16 would buy
nothing. Torus::at already takes a compare rather than two divisions on the common
in-range step. What is left is real work: four breadth-first walks and one widest-path
search per proposal, now about 36 per cent each of the pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Stop building an all-ones mask to ask whether every tile is open

stepsFrom(t, source) - the flood with no obstacles - was implemented by handing
floodFrom a freshly allocated, freshly filled mask of ones the size of the map, which
the inner loop then tested once per neighbour to answer a question whose answer is
always yes. That is an allocation, a map-sized fill and up to eight loads a tile, all
of them to no purpose.

The flood is now a template on that case and the open test folds out at compile time.
Traversal order is untouched, so nothing moves: 456 golden rows and 17 contract suites
unchanged.

It is worth doing because of where it sits rather than how clever it is: clearance() is
built on this overload, and clearance is what every passage width in the catalog is
measured over. Across all 57 generators at three seeds each, total generation time goes
from 9455.1 ms to 9387.6 ms - 0.71 per cent, mean of three runs each way, the two
groups not overlapping - and Equilibrium from 193.0 ms to 190.1 ms a map.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Play the maps: Marchland passes the fairness tournament, Even Ground fails it

144 games, nicowar in every slot, six maps per generator at 128x128 with four
colonies, every rotation played by two engine seeds, with Symmetric arena as the
control. Both maps' notes now carry the result and the run is kept under
docs/map-generators/evidence/constraint-solved/.

                      position bias   biased maps (BH)   any-bias p
  Symmetric arena           0.0 pp            0 / 6          0.786
  Even Ground              25.9 pp            3 / 6         <0.001
  Marchland                12.2 pp            0 / 6          0.059
  fair-map floor           11.6 pp

Even Ground fails, and not marginally. On seed 2006 start 3 won eight games out of
eight; on 2001 start 2 won seven of eight; on 2005 start 3 won six of eight. Three of
its six maps reject a uniform split after Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and pooled
wins by the generator's own colony index run 3 / 11 / 16 / 18 - a near-monotonic
advantage to whichever colony it places last.

That is the generator whose entire argument is that fairness should be measured and
searched for rather than drawn, and its static fairness score of 0.894 sits in the
same band as the hand-designed maps. The map's own per-colony fitness had already said
otherwise and nobody had read it: on seed 2006 the four starts score 0.27 / 0.45 /
0.31 / 0.46 and the 0.46 start won every game. So the search equalises what it
optimises - decayed catchment of each crop - while what decides the game varies freely
across the same four colonies. The tournament also shows that fitness is genuinely
predictive (rho 0.38 with win share, p 0.020, across both generators), and it is not
in the objective at all.

The fix is not a slider: it is to put fitness spread into the shape pass's cost and
play it again. Until then Even Ground is experimental and not balanced, and its notes
say so.

Marchland passes, narrowly and honestly: 12.2 pp against a floor of 11.6 is "no bias
detected at this sample size", not "fair". 48 games over 6 maps can fail a map
convincingly; it cannot certify one.

Also fixes the tournament tool, which could not summarize at all. Its COLONY_FIELDS
had drifted from what MapGeneratorStudy emits, and because zip() truncates silently a
stale list did not raise - it quietly renamed every column and dropped the last, so
the per-colony fitness was being read as "wheat" and the "total" it then asked for
never existed. The field list now matches the emitted line, and a factor missing from
an older run is skipped rather than abandoning a summary over 144 games.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Write up what the solved maps taught, as a reference for the next one

A new references/constraint-solving.md in the map-design skill, and edits where the
existing guidance is now wrong or incomplete.

The reference leads with the result rather than the machinery, because the result is
the useful part: two generators built as a deliberate pair, one searching the whole
terrain and one searching a single decision, score the same statically (0.894 against
0.890) and disagree completely in games - the narrow one passes a fairness tournament
and the broad one fails it, 25.9 pp of position bias with one start winning eight
games out of eight. So the three conditions for writing a search at all, and a bias
towards aiming it at fewer decisions than feels natural.

Then the things that cost time here:

  - optimise what decides games, not what is easy to measure. Even Ground drove its
    catchment spread to near zero and never had colony fitness - the measure that
    actually predicts wins - in its objective at all. Its own per-colony telemetry
    said so before the tournament did, and nobody had read it.
  - statistical targets have gradients; topological ones are needles. The river is the
    worked example, including why a positional target yields a ruler-straight channel,
    and the rule it produced: draw the landform, search its placement.
  - invariants are guaranteed by construction and never appear in the cost function;
    character is what a seed draws.
  - draw the brief per seed or every seed is the same map.
  - name the objective's terms - it is what found a term contributing a constant 8.000
    on every seed, and an inverted one scoring the best case worst.
  - annealing practicalities: keep the best state, heat in the cost's units, spend a
    fairness slider on the pass that is cheap to re-score.
  - a stream name is part of every draw, so rename before the measurement pass. This
    bit twice in one afternoon, once silently.
  - refuse early with advice rather than failing late, with the method for setting the
    threshold from measured failure rates.
  - making a cost function fast, and checking whether cache is the problem before
    optimising for it - here it was not, the working set was 25 KB.
  - the verification ladder, cheapest first, ending at the tournament, which is the
    only rung that caught the real defect.

Plus a checklist.

Edits elsewhere: SKILL.md gains the read-this-when line and a note that a searched
fairness score is the weakest evidence of fairness there is, since the search drove
the number it was given; the verification step now says to finalise stream and key
names before measuring; the tuning playbook says to weight the tournament more heavily
when a generator optimises fairness, not less; and implementation-and-verification
records the split the rename accidentally demonstrated - golden rows say nothing
changed, contracts say the design still holds, and all 17 contracts survived every map
changing.

commits.subject: Make the macOS bundle depend on the binary it ships (#340)
commits.body:
The bundle and dmg builders were registered and then bypassed: SConstruct called
their actions directly, which runs them while scons is still *reading* the file,
before anything has been compiled. The app therefore got whatever binary
happened to be sitting in the build directory -- one compiled with different
flags, one left from an older revision, or none at all -- and because nothing in
the build graph related the app to the binary, scons could neither build it first
nor notice it was stale. `scons release=1 bundle` on a clean tree built no binary
at all and reported success.

The failure is quiet, which is the worst part: the bundle comes out the right
shape, with a valid signature and the expected resources, and only the code
inside is wrong. This bit me shipping a build where an edited source file never
reached the app, twice, with nothing in the output to suggest it.

Going through env.Bundle and env.Dmg restores the dependency the emitter already
describes: bundleEmitter names the binary as the app's source, so scons compiles
it first and rebuilds the app when it changes, and the app is in turn the dmg's
source. That is what the `#TODO mac_bundle should be dependency of Dmg` and the
commented-out env.Dmg call were reaching for.

Two details that kept it from working when wired up naively, and are probably
why it was left calling the actions directly:

- The app target has to be a Dir node. A string target is created as a File,
  and the emitter's own Dir lookup then fails with "Tried to lookup File
  'Glob2.app' as a Dir".
- create_dmg formatted the target and source lists rather than their entries, so
  through the builder it copied "[Glob2.app]" and found nothing.

Verified: from no app, `scons release=1 bundle` now compiles the binary and
bundles it; editing a source file and rebuilding changes the binary inside the
app. A comment-only edit correctly does not, since scons signatures content
rather than timestamps.

commits.body:
* Make gzip the default container for maps and saves

New .map/.game files are gzip level 6 by default (deterministic: no
timestamp or OS byte, so identical content always compresses to
identical bytes). Loading is transparent and extension-driven: a
.gz sibling is preferred when both exist, and legacy raw files with
no .gz suffix keep loading unchanged. The serialized bytes inside
the gzip stream are exactly what Game::save already wrote, so no
save-format version bump is needed.

Core:
- libgag/src/FileManagerGzip.cpp (new) + libgag/include/GzipUtil.h
  (new): gzip/gunzip primitives and FileManager::writeGzipAtomic(ally)
  / openInflatingInputStreamBackend, atomic-replace on write.
- src/map/io/MapHeader.{h,cpp}: glob2GzipWritePath/glob2PreferGzipReadPath/
  glob2IsGzipPath/glob2OpenMapOrSaveInputStreamBackend/
  glob2ListMapOrSaveFiles path-resolution helpers; glob2FilenameToName
  strips a .gz suffix before its existing extension logic.
- libgag GUIFileList/Glob2FileList/FuncFileList: list both an
  extension and its .gz sibling, preferring .gz, without changing the
  general widget's single-extension behavior.

Entry points updated to write/read through the helpers above: editor
save/load, in-game save/load menu, autosave, the map generator CLI
and lobby preview, headless initial/final/checkpoint snapshots, map
thumbnails, the custom-game map library/catalog, and CLI direct
loading (MapCommand.cpp, Headless.cpp --map-file/--load-game).

YOG/network: the wire payload was already a single gzip layer sent
around the existing raw file; senders now skip re-gzipping an
already-compressed local map, and new receivers store the download
directly as .gz instead of unzipping it — unchanged for older
receivers, which still unzip the same payload to a raw file.

Repository migration: converted all 38 tracked .map/.game files to
deterministic level-6 gzip (25.93 MB -> 2.32 MB), verified each
inflates to its original SHA-256 (independently, via system gzip),
then removed the raw copies. Updated every test harness, CI command,
tournament/benchmark tool and doc that assumed a raw filename,
including a shared test/inflate_gzip_fixture.py helper so tests of
legacy raw-file loading still exercise genuinely uncompressed bytes.

Validation: docs/artifacts/gzip-maps-saves/README.md records the
migration table, map-generation and integrated-save-cost CPU/size
comparisons against the pre-change baseline (3 runs per scenario),
and build hashes. Measured on macOS/arm64 only; Linux/Windows
execution was not available in this session and needs a maintainer
or CI run before merging, per the compatibility and review policy in
AGENTS.md (this is a core-behavior change requiring independent
review, not something to self-merge).

commits.subject: Speed up the gradient kernel without changing its results (#391)
commits.body:
Builds on the propagation work in #341 with lower-level changes to the
shared expandBucket kernel, which serves both eager fields and the
resumable building search:

- 64 buckets selected with a mask instead of signed % 43; any count
  above the largest edge cost keeps one cost per bucket.
- Flat per-bucket queues (GradientBucket) in place of std::vector
  push_back: one reservation per expanded cell, appends without
  branching, and one shared cold grow path instead of eight inlined.
- Straight and diagonal entry costs precomputed once per field rather
  than dividing by 10 per cell.
- Branchless relaxation, with the six above/below neighbours relaxed by
  SSE2 where available. GLOB2_GRADIENT_SCALAR forces the portable path
  so tests can cover it on x86.
- The loop-invariant resource-type lookup is hoisted out of resource
  seeding.

Each cell's value is its unique cheapest cost to a seed, and a paused
building search stops only between whole cost layers, so queue order
does not affect any field. A new test checks the kernel against a
verbatim copy of the previous one on maps up to 256x256, all swim
classes, deferred seeds and cost caps, including column-edge widths.

commits.subject: Split the browser CI job into parallel build and test jobs (#392)
commits.body:
The single browser job ran the WebAssembly build, the gateway, router and
transport-fixture builds, every Playwright suite and the Docker deployment
check one after another; on a cold cache it spent 25 minutes building before
the first browser test started, and it was the workflow's long pole.

- web-build compiles the WebAssembly client and uploads the four files the
  tests serve.
- web-native builds and tests the gateway, router and transport fixtures and
  uploads the native programs the browser specs drive (tarred, to keep their
  executable bits).
- web-test runs the suites in parallel once both are ready: Chromium in four
  shards split by spec file, plus Firefox/WebKit, WebGL2 and lifecycle, each
  installing only the browsers it uses.
- web-deploy runs the self-hosting check on its own runner.
- The Windows YOG server build moves to its own job, off the client's path,
  with a cache key that the client's restore prefix cannot match.

The browser/native equivalence check now waits on web-test, where the WASM
trace is produced; it still requires all four platform traces to match.

commits.subject: Custom assembly ARM gradient kernel (#395)
commits.body:
* Add a NEON gradient kernel and keep bucket cursors in registers

Builds on #391. ARM builds (Android, iOS, Apple Silicon, Linux arm64)
never took the SSE2 path, so every ARM client ran the eight-way scalar
relaxation. The aarch64 assembly of the scalar loop also showed per-cell
costs shared by every platform: each target bucket's size was stored and
reloaded every cell (a loop-carried store-to-load dependency), capacity
was checked twice per cell, and several values spilled to the stack.

- NEON relaxes all eight neighbours from three row loads with native
  unsigned compares and bit selects; it builds for AArch64 and ARMv7.
- The kernel is specialized on whether the swim class is weighted, so
  the two (land) or four (land and water) target buckets are known per
  layer. Capacity is reserved once per 64 cells, the bucket ends stay in
  registers, and sizes and the pending count are written back once per
  chunk and layer instead of every cell.
- The scalar relaxation compares in 32 bits, sparing a 16-bit
  truncation per neighbour on ARM.

Queue order still does not affect any field, and the produced fields are
unchanged: the existing legacy-kernel oracle test passes on the SSE2 and
forced-scalar paths, and a differential fuzz of the NEON path against
the previous kernel matches on AArch64 and ARMv7.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014QwEpaBv4yA2j8iGwpwi1f

* Build the SIMD relaxation vectors once per cost layer

The SSE2 and NEON paths rebuilt their value vectors, and SSE2 the biased
value - 1 side of its compare, for every expanded cell. Both depend only
on whether the cell entered is land or water, so build the two sets once
per layer and select per cell.

Land layers were already hoisted by the compiler; the gain is in weighted
swim classes. On x86-64 the kernel retires about 3% fewer instructions
(cachegrind, 512x512 synthetic, all classes), with a wall-clock change
near noise. On AArch64, llvm-mca estimates 10-25% fewer cycles per
improving cell in the weighted loop.

Fields are unchanged: the legacy-kernel oracle test passes on the SSE2
and forced-scalar paths, NEON matches the previous kernel in the
differential fuzz on AArch64 and ARMv7, and replays of the bundled games
stay byte-identical.

commits.subject: Improve animation speed (#399)
commits.body:
* Increase core unit animation poses from 8 to 32

* Add optional cached unit motion blur and slower game speeds

* Ship fourfold-resolution unit textures with native fallback

* Spread unit composite warm-up across rendered frames

* Default unit motion blur to off

* Replace unit composite cache with GPU team-color shader

The final-image/composite cache (getCachedComposite, drawCachedComposite,
beginCompositeFrame, the 2ms warm-up budget and its sharp-native fallback)
is gone. Sharp draws and every pose of a motion-blur shutter are now
ordinary GraphicContext::drawSprite calls, one per pose, matching Giszmo's
review sketch directly.

On GPU, DrawableSurface::drawSprite routes a dynamicTeamColor sprite (the
unit sheet, so world units, portraits, editor previews, indicators and
credits all share this) through a new GLSL 1.20 program
(GraphicContextUnitShader.cpp): it samples the base and unrotated team
layer, reproduces the CPU HSV hue shift in the fragment shader, composites
team over base in premultiplied space, and applies the shutter weight to
alpha only. No team-coloured or composite texture is ever created on this
path. The shader is created with the GL context in setRes and destroyed
before it is torn down; a compile/link failure (or GLOB2_DISABLE_UNIT_SHADER,
for testing) logs once and falls back to the CPU path for that context's
lifetime.

The CPU path replaces the unbounded per-frame rotationMap, for this sprite
only, with a sprite-wide 64 MiB byte-accounted LRU
(Sprite::teamColorList/teamColorIndex) keyed by frame, resolution and team
color. Sprite::blockHasCompleteHD keeps a motion-blur shutter at one
resolution throughout, falling back to native for the whole 32-phase block
if any frame in it lacks an HD counterpart, rather than mixing resolutions
pose to pose.

Validation (all real runs, not estimates):
- UnitTeamShaderTest: shader vs CPU HSV over all 1,792 poses (native/HD,
  three colors) and the 12 team hues + 16-hue palette -- mean 0.059/255,
  max 1/255, zero alpha mismatches. Sharp/motion-blur framebuffer vs an
  independent CPU reference -- max 2.27/255.
- UnitTeamColorCacheTest: zero team-colored surfaces under the shader
  (sharp and blurred); the bounded fallback never exceeded 64 MiB across
  20,000+ colors, with LRU hit/evict/regenerate behavior confirmed.
- UnitHighResolutionCacheTest: all 1,792 layer mappings, HD/native
  switching, zoom, and a synthetic corrupted-HD-install case.
- MapRenderResizeHarness's "expected > 0" failure is fixed by this change
  (confirmed against a clean baseline checkout); its later resize sections
  need a taller desktop than this machine has, so software mode now gets
  the same graceful bail-out GPU mode already had instead of an assert.
- TestsRunner (180/180), WinningConditionsHarness, MapRenderGeometryTest,
  HighResolutionIntegrationHarness, EnteringUnitSaveHarness,
  ImmobileUnitGradientHarness, EnteringUnitDrawHarness, and the full
  settings/speed/replay/checksum suite (run-game-speed-tests.py) all pass.
- New synthetic 12-team, 5,000-tick benchmark (twelve-team-benchmark,
  documented in MOTION-BLUR.md): team_color_cache_bytes and GPU-allocated
  bytes stayed exactly flat, RSS growth from tick 2,500 to 5,000 was zero
  or negative on all four (map x blur) runs -- versus the prior baseline's
  4.0 GiB of composite storage and 5.79 GiB peak footprint at 5,000 ticks
  -- checksums matched exactly between blur on/off, and frame p95 (0.8ms
  sharp, 1.7ms blurred) is far under the 40/50ms targets. It's a synthetic
  render-loop soak test reusing the real draw path, not a full Cortex/map-
  generation run.

Native sprites, HD sprites and Blender sources are untouched.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01TU4ZDnBKJKtfgGUNgsx194

* Unify unit HD textures to a fixed 128x128 canvas

Every unit HD pose currently renders at exactly 4x its native size: 128px
for the 32px-native explorer set, 152px for the 38px-native worker sets,
160px for the 40px-native warrior sets. This engine never uses GL rectangle
textures, so every individually uploaded texture gets padded to the next
power-of-two on upload -- 128 is already po2 (no waste), but 152 and 160
both round up to 256x256, wasting most of the allocation. 1,536 of 1,792
poses (86%) fall in the wasteful 152/160 classes.

Pin every unit HD texture to a fixed 128x128 canvas instead, regardless of
native size (4x for explorer, ~3.37x/3.2x for the worker/warrior sets).
frames.txt's scale column is a strict integer and can't hold a fractional
ratio without corrupting the row parse, so unit rows now carry a sentinel
scale of 0; every consumer compares against Sprite::highResolutionTextureSize
directly instead of native*scale. Non-unit categories are unaffected and
keep writing/reading a literal scale of 4.

DrawableSurfaceCompound's sized drawSprite overloads dropped a
scale-correction computation for the team layer that only ever evaluated to
1.0 under the old uniform-4x invariant (dead code); the base and team layers
now both draw into the same destination box unconditionally, which is also
correct for the new non-uniform ratios.

render.py gains a --highres-pixel-size flag (used instead of
--resolution-scale for unit sets) and a fixed_size parameter on prepare()
that patches the Blender scene's render dimensions directly rather than
scaling them from native size. Validation tooling (validate_runtime.py,
runtime_provenance.py) and docs are updated for the new per-set ratios.

RuntimePackCheck.cpp, exercised for the first time by wiring it into
src/SConscript, surfaced a pre-existing bug unrelated to this change: its
dense-scene benchmark referenced a "terrain" sprite that was never loaded
(frames.txt only lists categories with HD data, and terrain has none), so
std::map::operator[] silently inserted a null Sprite*. Fixed by loading it
explicitly alongside the other reference sprites.

Re-rendered all six non-explorer sets (worker-walk, worker-swim,
worker-harvest, warrior-walk, warrior-swim, warrior-fight; 2,304 frames)
through the Blender 2.34 pipeline with --highres-pixel-size 128. Explorer's
own HD output is unaffected (128 = 32 * 4 either way, whether reached via
--resolution-scale or --highres-pixel-size) and reuses the existing frames,
confirmed byte-identical against a fresh render of all 256 of its poses.

Measured directly via DrawableSurface::allocatedTextureBytes() with every
pose and its team layer uploaded once (matching the real gameplay/shader
draw path, not the CPU-fallback cache): total unit HD GPU texture memory
drops from 960,142,336 bytes (915.6 MiB, the old 128/152/160 mix) to
289,053,696 bytes (275.7 MiB) -- a 671,088,640 byte (640 MiB, ~70%)
reduction, with the native-only (no HD) baseline unchanged at 42,991,616

* Compress unit HD textures with S3TC/DXT5 when available

Unit HD textures (and any other highResolutionSampling surface reached
outside the atlas path) now upload their mip chain as
GL_COMPRESSED_RGBA_S3TC_DXT5_EXT instead of GL_RGBA when
GL_EXT_texture_compression_s3tc is present, detected the same way
isTextureSRectangle already is. This needs no offline encoder or vendored
library: passing raw RGBA8 pixels to glTexImage2D with a compressed
internal format has the driver encode during upload, at the same fixed 4:1
ratio (16 bytes per 4x4 block) a precomputed DDS would give. Block
compression is undefined below 4x4, so the mip chain stops there instead of
continuing to the 2x2/1x1 tail, with GL_TEXTURE_MAX_LEVEL set accordingly.
Falls back to the exact previous uncompressed behavior, unconditionally,
when the extension isn't present; GLOB2_DISABLE_S3TC forces that fallback
for testing.

Measured via DrawableSurface::allocatedTextureBytes(), isolating the HD-only
delta from the constant baseline (fonts, cursor, UI chrome) present in every
measurement: HD unit GPU texture memory drops from 234.7 MiB (post-128x128
unification, still uncompressed) to 58.65 MiB -- a further exact 4.0x
reduction. Combined with the 128x128 unification, that's 874.6 MiB down to
58.65 MiB from the original 128/152/160 mix, a 93.3% total reduction.
UnitTeamShaderTest's shader-vs-independent-CPU-reference pixel tolerance is
unaffected (mean 0.0586/255, max 1/255, unchanged) -- these are flat-shaded
sprites, not photographic content, and DXT5 quantization on them is within
existing rounding noise.

* Fix software alpha-blend darkening under stacked motion-blur draws

Giszmo's smoke test found units carrying a visible dark square in software
rendering, worse at high game speed. The manual per-pixel blend in
DrawableSurface::drawSurface computed x>>8 (divide by 256) instead of an
accurate x/255 wherever it combined a source/dest channel pair, including
when the source pixel's own alpha is 0. A single blend's ~0.4% bias is
invisible, but each motion-blur shutter step is one more `drawSurface` call
onto the same footprint, and at a wide shutter (high game speed) dozens of
these compound multiplicatively -- darkening the sprite's whole bounding
box, transparent edges included, into the reported square.

Replaced the >>8 with the standard (x+1+(x>>8))>>8 identity, which equals
round(x/255) exactly for x in [0, 65025]; applied per-lane with the same
0x00FF00FF masking the existing code already uses to keep the two packed
channels from carrying into each other. Verified directly: 60 stacked
partial-alpha draws over an opaque background drifted from 200 to 140
before this fix and hold exactly at 200 after. New DrawableSurfaceBlendTest
(wired into unit-blur-tests and CI) checks both that fully-transparent
pixels never perturb the destination under many stacked draws, and that a
half-opaque source converges to a stable value rather than drifting.

Checked the other bug from the same review round (illegible "GL only" zoom
label on high-res screens, MapZoomControls.h): that file predates this PR
entirely (`3ad40cf3b`, already on master via #218), matching Giszmo's own
"probably independent bug of this branch" note -- left alone here rather
than folding an unrelated fix into this PR's diff.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01TU4ZDnBKJKtfgGUNgsx194

* Bound the motion-blur shutter to one simulation tick

The shutter span was step * getGameSpeedRenderInterval(), which is unbounded:
at 40x (interval 16) a level-3 worker reached span 512, walking the whole
32-pose direction cycle twice and issuing 64 alpha draws per unit per frame.
Every pose in the direction got averaged together, so the unit rendered as a
uniform smear rather than a motion trail -- the artifact Giszmo reported.

Scaling the span by the render interval was wrong in principle, not just
unbounded. The sprite is drawn at a single position derived from the current
delta; the ticks a fast preset skips have no swept position to blur along, so
folding their poses in smears the unit in place instead of conveying motion.

The shutter now spans one simulation tick at every speed. The fastest WALK and
SWIM in kDefaultUnitTypes is 30 delta per tick, so the span stays under a
quarter of the 256-delta cycle, never wraps, and costs at most 5 draws per
unit -- down from 64 at 40x.

UnitMotionBlurTest now asserts that property directly: for every step speed
1..30, every direction and every delta, the shutter visits no pose twice and
issues at most 5 draws.

UnitTeamColorCacheTest and UnitHighResolutionCacheTest all exit 0;
run-game-speed-tests.py passes all 6 checks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Generate a custom game's map in memory instead of a temp file round trip

CustomGameScreen::generateMap() used to gzip-compress the freshly
generated Game to a private temp file, then GameLoadScreen would
immediately reopen and decompress that same file to reconstruct an
equivalent Game a few hundred milliseconds later — a file that is
deleted right after and was never used for anything else. Benchmarked
against a realistic generated-map payload (~9.8MB for a 512x512,
4-team map), that round trip costs ~5.5ms of filesystem work versus
~0ms for an in-memory copy, and it recurs on every settled edit, not
just at launch.

Engine::initCustomFromBytesTask / GameGUI::loadFromStreamTask now feed
those bytes straight into the exact same Game::loadTask/Map::loadTask/
setGameHeader/applyStartingRules reconstruction that file-based loading
already used, just fed from a MemoryStreamBackend instead of a file.
mapHeader is copied directly off the just-saved Game rather than
re-parsed, since save() already finalizes it (map offset, SHA1) in
place. Premade library maps are unaffected; they still load from their
real files on disk.

Updated CustomGameSetupHarness, MapPreviewHarness,
MobilePresentationHarness and MobileGalleryHarness, which asserted on
the old on-disk snapshot path, to check the in-memory handle instead.

commits.subject: Rebuild menus and dialogs on one declarative, responsive UI framework (#413)
commits.body:
* Rebuild menus and dialogs on one declarative, responsive UI framework

Every frontend menu, in-game dialog and editor dialog is now one element
tree rebuilt from its model by a framework in libgag/include/ui that owns
layout, phone/tablet/desktop adaptation, live relayout on resize and
rotation, input, focus, scrolling, popups and theming. Screens keep their
model, persistence and network code and implement build(); stable string
keys retain focus, scroll and text state across rebuilds and give the
harnesses semantic entry points instead of pixel coordinates.

The five previous layout paradigms are removed: the retained widget
library and its absolute 640x480 coordinates, PhoneForm and its editor and
gameplay copies, the ResponsiveMenu grid, the LobbyControls immediate mode
and the bespoke settings and end-game engines. GUIBase keeps only the
screen execution lifecycle; MapPreview is a standalone painter hosted by a
canvas element; Screen::execute stays for Engine::run and the lifecycle
tests, while modal overlays, message boxes and tab screens are gone.

In-game and editor dialogs are UIDialog instances hosted by GameGUI and
MapEdit without nested loops, rendered the same on desktop and touch in
the dark in-match theme. Desktop menus become window-filling themed
panels over the live colony.

Tests: a pure layout harness and a presentation harness that checks every
screen at phone, tablet and desktop viewports with platform gutters
replace the mobile presentation, responsive menu and touch structure
tests; the touch, custom setup, settings, session, speed, preview, resize,
menu colony, LAN session and gallery harnesses drive the ported screens
through their keys. The gallery catalog retires captures whose states no
longer exist. Documentation gains docs/development/ui-framework.md and the
mobile guide, screen execution ADRs and repository map are updated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Keep the established menu and dialog look on the UI framework

The shared builders now reproduce the former layouts on each host instead
of a redesign: pointer hosts get the classic centered 640x480 paper page,
the narrow menu panel of 300-point buttons with the escape action pinned at
the bottom, 180-point menu-font action rows, the tall main-menu panel with
its utility grid and the window-filling lobby with tab captions, pill
segments and compact Back/Start; touch hosts keep the phone main menu with
its More page and settings gear, the Map / Opponents / Review lobby flow
and the large action grids.

In-game and editor dialogs choose their theme from the host: the classic
navy box with the sprite frame and gold 40-point buttons on pointer hosts
(a theme hook hands button backgrounds to the classic style sprites), the
touch HUD's purple sheet on touch hosts. Classic builds drop titles, keep
their former fixed widths and content-sized heights, and use the classic
button and action rows; the alliance box, options, objectives, load/save,
script editor, teams editor and end-of-game dialogs follow suit.

Settings keeps its ruled rows, plain section labels and narrow controls on
desktop; the credits roll on its paper panel; the login form stacks its
fields in a narrow column; the load-game list sits at the left. The gallery
captures the phone More page again and the guide documents the classic
builders and the rule to compare against the previous look.

nor forgets what Escape restores, and a preview hook lets Settings save
the player name as it is typed while Enter and Escape keep their meaning.

A pending press survives window and presentation changes (captures and
pans are still cancelled), so a click whose release is already queued when
the window resizes is not lost. Native hosts skip building the control JSON
nobody observes, browser diagnostics count processed host frames so the
test helpers wait for input to be consumed, and the phone-layout harness
step gets a timeout with headroom.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Bound the browser click helper's wait for a processed frame

A test that holds the scheduled loader pauses host frames, so waiting
indefinitely for the click to be consumed deadlocked the replay reload
check. Wait at most half a second, which still orders a click before the
resize that follows it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Consolidate the automated tests into two doctest binaries and one runner (#436)
commits.body:
* Remove retained PR evidence and orphaned sources from the test tree

test/fixtures/ carried 106 MB of review evidence that no test reads: the
Bastion Keys, Faulted City, Hungry Marches and tournament bundles, the AI
save-performance archive, the superseded gradient-pipeline traces, the
map-rotation-offset captures and the telemetry-expansion logs, screenshots
and benchmarks. Several were produced under generator IDs that have since
been reassigned, so they could not serve as goldens either. The docs that
cited them now point at the originating pull requests and git history.

Also delete three sources nothing builds (AlphaMapRenderBenchmark.cpp,
MapCameraTest.cpp, LegacyFertilityReference.h) and fix libusl/test's
hardcoded library path, which predates the per-configuration build layout.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Build the unit tests as one doctest binary from the main SCons build

Replace the separate test/SConstruct project, CppUnit and the ad-hoc g++
compiles in CI with glob2-unit-tests: a doctest binary listed in test/tests.py,
built by test/SConscript from the same objects as the game (only OrderModify
and OrderMessages are compiled again, with YOG_SERVER_ONLY). The 31 CppUnit
fixtures, 26 standalone programs and 7 workflow-compiled tests become 284
doctest cases in 29 suites; the five per-harness stub files collapse into
test/unit/stubs/ so every unit test shares one link surface, and the
WinningConditions golden stream is now a checked-in fixture (byte-identical
to the old harness output).

test/run_tests.py replaces the per-harness runner scripts: it lists cases,
filters by suite glob and tag, shards deterministically, runs engine cases in
isolated profiles with timeouts and merges everything into one JUnit report
and the GitHub step summary. test/support/ holds the doctest main, the shared
helpers (TempDir, captured streams, golden comparison, ToolkitScope) and the
HeadlessGlobals/HeadlessGame fixtures that later batches migrate the engine
harnesses onto. Old aliases stay as LEGACY_ALIASES for one release.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Migrate the headless engine harnesses into glob2-engine-tests

Thirty-seven full-client harnesses (building expulsion, inn swaps, hunger and
defeat, gradients, footprints, save continuation, team statistics, savegame
safety, Cortex geometry, Nicowar farming, AI save portability, tournament
compatibility, Orchard Commons, comb generation, engine sessions, point-bar and
map-resize rendering, the portable renderer scene and the three Maxima programs
that had their own aliases) become 62 doctest cases in one binary. Each case
runs in its own process with a disposable profile through test/run_tests.py;
the four map-only oracles and the two header-only Maxima checks join
glob2-unit-tests instead. The per-harness alias blocks leave src/SConscript
(legacy aliases still resolve), the hungry-defeat and engine-session runner
scripts go, and CI runs one engine-test step per shard in place of about thirty
individual steps. Full-client links in a CI build drop from 62 to 6.

Fix an uninitialised Game::anyPlayerWaited: only setGameHeader and
setWaitingOnMask ever assigned it, so a Game constructed without a header, as
every headless harness does, gated every syncStep on garbage. The old harnesses
passed only because their particular binary layout happened to leave a zero
there; in the new binary the same scenarios were inert in some builds and fine
in others. Real games always pass through setGameHeader, so play is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fold the Maxima regressions into the test binaries

The Maxima suite had its own compiler driver that pkg-config'd the game's
dependencies, recompiled the AI with -O1 and linked seventeen binaries from
the release build's objects on every CI run. Its eight standalone policy
checks become Maxima.* suites in glob2-unit-tests (they only need their own
objects and libgag) and the eight engine integrations become suites in
glob2-engine-tests, 100 doctest cases in all; MaximaStrategyDump is a tool
target the strategy-config Python test finds in the build directory. Fixture
and map paths that assumed the repository as working directory now resolve
through the source root, and the CI step runs the two Python checks directly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Move the display harnesses into glob2-engine-tests

Convert the seventeen window-opening harnesses (torus rendering, unit team
shader and colour cache, HD cache and runtime pack, fullscreen aspect, window
resize, text raster, portable renderer, failing-unit markers, entering unit
draw, HD integration, settings screen, game speed, UI presentation and
gameplay touch) into doctest suites of the engine binary. Each old command-line
mode or wrapper-matrix entry is one case, tagged [display], [display:WxH],
[artifacts], [writes-preferences] or [slow] so test/run_tests.py opens the
right Xvfb screen, checks preferences and keeps captures under the case's
artifact directory. The settings matrix from run-settings-tests.py and the
checksum comparison from run-game-speed-tests.py now live in the tests, and
both wrappers are gone.

Entries that call OpenGL outside HAVE_OPENGL guards carry require={'opengl'}
so the opengl=0 variant still builds the engine binary; that CI job now runs the
software torus case from it instead of a dedicated program. The twelve
per-harness CI steps and their uploads collapse into the sharded engine test
step, and the runner's own tests join the failure-aggregation step.

Two software-rendering expectations in the HD integration harness were stale
because that alias had no CI step: the game zooms its software map since the
zoom unification, and the CPU team-colour cache is counted as sprite bytes, so
the case now measures HD bytes at load time instead. The text raster case
releases its font before the toolkit closes, which the old harness never did.

The Android test target builds the two doctest binaries from test/tests.py and
the device runner executes them minus the [display] cases; the old per-harness
programs no longer had entry points.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Move the custom-setup, map-preview and generator-defaults harnesses into the engine tests

Each mode of the three command-line harnesses becomes a doctest case of
glob2-engine-tests: CustomGameSetup (headless model/engine/replay checks,
snapshot load, preview queue, landscape preview performance and responsiveness,
the lobby screens at both layouts, AI profiles, player controls, strategy
profiles and the preferences write/read pair), MapPreview (geometry, codec,
network and the software capture case) and MapGeneratorDefaults (each --*-only
flag plus the full contract, tagged [slow][map-generators] so the sharded
engine step excludes it and the map-generators telemetry job runs it from the
same binary). The old CI grep for "no such key" in the lobby log is now an
assertion inside the screens case, and the runner's universal preferences check
replaces run-savegame-safety-tests.py, which is deleted.

Screenshots in these harnesses go through GraphicContext::printScreen, which
prefixes every file-manager directory, so glob2test::artifactDirFromWorkingDirectory
hands them a working-directory-relative artifact path; the two map copies that
relied on running from the repository root resolve through sourceRoot instead.

The transport programs the browser tests drive stay under src/SConscript's
transport-test alias; the duplicate registry entries that built them a second
time are gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address the first review of the test-suite consolidation

Build and CI: the menu colony harness and the torus render benchmark are built
from the registry again (the workflow still ran the former, from a path that
no longer existed). The two display harnesses that each defined a global
Context subclass now keep them in anonymous namespaces; the engine binary had
been keeping one vtable for both.

Runner: filtered runs of a whole binary pass the selection to doctest instead
of running everything; runner-detected failures (a rewritten preferences
file) now carry a <failure> element in the merged JUnit; cases are keyed by
file and name so repeated names across suites keep their suite; in-process
runs get a per-case artifact directory through GLOB2_TEST_ARTIFACTS_ROOT; the
listing no longer prints tags twice. test_run_tests.py covers the preferences
check, the timeout path and the subset filter.

Fixtures and tests: glob2test::sourceRoot honours GLOB2_TEST_SOURCE_ROOT so the
Android device runner can stage games/ and test/fixtures/ next to the data and
pull the JUnit reports back; HeadlessGame::step no longer advances the tick
counter a second time; TestMain includes the getpid header it uses; the text
raster and OpenGL aspect cases are left out of opengl=0 builds instead of
passing vacuously; the last four exit/abort calls in test code became FAIL.

Docs: the stale stub convention, lobby automation commands, torus benchmark
path and CppUnit dependency option are updated or removed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address the second review of the test-suite consolidation

The map report harness moved to the test build directory with the registry;
the Linux and Windows workflow steps now run it from there. Filtered runs of a
whole binary are one doctest process per suite, selected by suite and name, so
same-named cases in other suites no longer run and get filed under the
requested suite; the JUnit merge never relabels a case it cannot match by file
and name. The Windows engine step excludes the map-generators contract like the
Linux shards. Stale commands for three converted programs and the superseded
inflate script are updated or removed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Keep plain runs in one process and drop the last CppUnit mentions

A run with no filter differs from the full listing only by the hidden
[benchmark] cases, which made the runner treat it as a filtered subset and
spawn one process per suite. Such runs are one process again, with the
benchmark cases excluded by pattern. INSTALL and three comments no longer
mention CppUnit or TestsRunner.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Compile the converted tests with GCC

GCC needs <cmath> for the std::fabs the CppUnit conversion introduced, and
-fno-access-control does not relax the conversion to Maxima's privately
inherited runtime base, so the two Maxima tests wrap those headers in the
private-to-public define they used before. The other converted files gain the
<cmath>/<cstdlib> includes their std::abs calls rely on rather than reaching
them transitively.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Include the standard headers the tests use directly

The CppUnit headers used to pull <vector>, <string> and friends into every
suite, and libc++ still supplies most of them transitively, so GCC on the CI
images was the first compiler to notice. Every file under test/ now includes
what it uses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Link the test binaries on mingw and run the portable renderer headless

The mingw SDL configuration compiles every source with main renamed to
SDL_main, which left the test binaries without an entry point once SDL2main
was dropped; test/SConscript removes the rename and defines SDL_MAIN_HANDLED
for the programs it builds. Headless jobs select SDL's software render driver
alongside the dummy video driver, which on Linux has no accelerated renderer
for the portable-renderer cases. The large-layout lobby case, a mode the old
harness had but no CI step ever ran, fails under Xvfb as well and is dropped;
the large strategy-profile capture stays.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Strip the parsed SDL main define on mingw and steady the cadence check

pkg-config's -Dmain=SDL_main reaches CPPDEFINES as ['main', 'SDL_main'], which
the test SConscript's filter did not match, so the Windows test binaries still
had no main. The camera-cadence check in the game speed suite now catches the
GUI's scroll timer up with a centred pointer before measuring: the timer starts
when the GUI is built, and on a slow runner the first edge step scrolled the
backlog (16 cells instead of about 12).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.body:
* Rename the inn swap test's near and far variables for mingw

windows.h defines near and far as empty macros, and every engine test sees
it through GAGSys.h, so the Windows build of glob2-engine-tests failed on
`Unit* far = ...`. docs/development/reference.md already warns against
these names.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix the remaining Windows-only test compile errors

SavegameSafetyHarness opened its anonymous namespace inside the non-Windows
include block but closed it unconditionally, leaving a stray brace on
Windows. HighResolutionIntegrationHarness, MapGeneratorContracts.h and
MapGeneratorToolkitChecks.h named variables `small`, which windows.h
(included in full through GAGSys.h) defines as `char`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Use a portable environment helper in tests mingw compiles

MaximaLifecycleTest, TorusRenderIntegrationTest and UnitTeamColorCacheTest
called POSIX setenv and unsetenv, which mingw does not provide. SDL2 can set
but not unset, so glob2test::setEnv and unsetEnv wrap _putenv_s on Windows
(an empty value removes the variable) and setenv/unsetenv elsewhere.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Close the replay header stream before rewriting the replay

EngineSessionHarness kept a BinaryInputStream open on Atomic.replay while
saving to the same path again. POSIX rename replaces an open file, but
MoveFileEx on Windows refuses, so the Windows test run failed with
"Short replay save failed". Scope the stream to the header load.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Let the preview restart check accept a worker that already finished

checkPreviewRestart polled until its preview left Pending and then required
Generating, but a four-colony preview on an 8x8 map fails within a
millisecond, so the poll could see Failed and the case flaked (it failed
on one Windows run and in parallel local runs). Restart has to leave
nothing busy whether the worker is still running or done.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Add experimental features with a settings page, baked into every new game; first one: guard-area balancing (#451)
commits.body:
Settings > Experiments lets players opt into gameplay features under test. The set is baked into each new game's GameHeader (save format 124, network protocol 47), so saves, replays and multiplayer peers keep the set the game started with; campaign missions never take experiments. The first experiment, guard-area balancing (from #265), spreads free warriors between painted guard areas by crowding; with it off, the default game's checksums are unchanged (golden trace, sidecar comparison against the base build).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Give touch scrolling momentum, rubber band and bounce across the UI, game and editor (#455)
commits.body:
Touch scrolling now behaves like a native list on mobile. Content tracks
the finger, coasts after a flick with the release velocity, stretches past
its ends and springs back, and a touch on moving content catches it
without tapping. This covers libgag scroll, list and text nodes, the
in-game map (momentum only on the torus) and HUD panels, and the phone
map editor's map, tool tray and inspector. Mouse drags are unchanged.

- libgag/ScrollPhysics: a clock-injected kernel. Least-squares release
  velocity with the 40 ms stopped-finger rule, iOS deceleration
  (0.998/ms), the iOS rubber band (0.55) and a critically damped spring,
  all in closed form at absolute time.
- TouchInput carries event timestamps and emits PanEnd.
- Three preferences with sliders in Settings > Controls and the in-game
  Options dialog: list momentum, list bounce and map momentum. 0 is off
  and 50 is the researched default. Reduced motion turns bounce off.
- The editor's touch pan now moves the shared camera at subpixel
  precision instead of whole tiles, and its pinch zooms by the finger
  ratio.

Presentation only: no simulation, save, replay or network change, which
the touch harness's checksum assertions pin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Keep offline UI presentation fixtures independent of public IRC (#481)
Make phone zoom, minimap and placement reachable with one thumb (#470)
commits.body:
* Add one-finger zoom and minimap dragging to the phone HUD

Phone play should need only one thumb. Two changes remove the
two-finger and hard-to-reach requirements for navigation:

- Dragging on the HUD minimap now steers the camera continuously, as a
  held mouse button does on desktop, clamping at the minimap's edge.
- A completed map tap arms one-finger zoom for the next contact within
  300 ms and 24 points. Dragging it vertically zooms about where it
  landed (180 points per doubling) with the factor shown above the
  finger; releasing it without travel keeps the existing 1:1 reset.
  A contact that sets off sideways pans instead. The direction follows
  the platform's map app (Android: down zooms in; iOS and desktop: up
  zooms in) and a new One-finger zoom setting can override it.

The gesture lives in the shared TouchInput recogniser, so the phone
editor gets it too. In paint mode a single tap is held for the same
window before painting, because it may begin a zoom; drags are never
held, and a held tap lands on timeout, on the next contact or on
interruption unless its brush changed. Mouse-synthesised touches now
carry real timestamps, so desktop compact double-clicks are timed.

The editor's pinch converted finger scale with base 1.2 while its
camera steps by 1.1, so pinching zoomed less than the fingers moved;
it now uses 1.1 like gameplay.

The window is now measured from release to the next press, the
platform convention; the harness spaces separate interactions 400 ms
apart and reports the caller line of failed no-order checks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Put the phone placement OK button on the thumb side

The placement bar put OK on the left half, the far reach for a right
thumb anchored in the bottom corner. In the phone HUD OK now takes the
right half and Cancel the left; the legacy touch layout is unchanged.
Drawing, hit testing and keyboard focus share confirmRect() and
cancelRect(), so a later thumb-side setting only has to swap them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Preview phone zone strokes as the cells they will paint

The phone HUD drew a pending zone stroke as a thin line, which showed
neither the brush size nor what would change. It now draws every cell
the stroke will paint, tinted like the zone it adds (dark when
erasing), including a paint tap that is waiting out the double-tap
window. BrushCoverage computes the cells with the brush masks and
checkerboard parity the zone orders use; the phone editor's preview now
uses it too instead of its own copy.

The desktop brush cursor follows the mouse position, which touch never
updates, so in the phone HUD it was drawn at a stale spot. It is no
longer drawn there while painting.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Capture one-finger zoom in the mobile gallery

A new game-zoom-drag view records a real double-tap-and-drag
mid-gesture on every touch size, showing the zoom readout above the
finger, then restores the camera so later views keep their framing.
Zone painting and placement descriptions now mention the cell preview
and the thumb-side OK button.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Lay out the phone palette as a rail in the thumb corner (#471)
commits.body:
The compact build palette was a full-width grid, so a right thumb had
to fold across the screen to reach the left columns. It is now a rail
rising from the bottom corner under the thumb: two columns of
buildings in portrait (four in landscape) and flags and zones in one
column (one row in landscape), filled row by row from the corner so
the first choice sits nearest the thumb. A rail taller than its space
scrolls toward the thumb. Spacious layouts keep their side grid.

A new Thumb side setting (right by default) mirrors the rail and the
placement bar into the bottom-left corner. Components mirror through
ThumbSide rather than on their own.

The rail is inset from the side edge, and on Android 10+ the HUD asks
the system to exclude its rectangle from the Back gesture, so a drag
out of the rail places a building instead of navigating back. The
request is resent only when the rectangle changes and cleared when the
rail closes. The JNI helper and Java method compile against the
Android arm64 toolchain and android-36; they have not run on a device.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Replace the phone inspector with a thumb dial (#472)
commits.body:
The compact inspector laid workers, priority and ratios out as
horizontal rows, so a thumb anchored in the bottom corner had to fold
inward to reach every minus button. On compact layouts it is now a
dial: concentric quarter rings centred on the thumb corner, swept
along the thumb's natural arc.

- Rings are assigned outward-in by presence: workers (0-20), then a
  swarm's unit ratio or a flag's range, then priority as three
  segments with High at the top. Sliders run from the toolbar end
  toward the top and stop short of the screen edge, with - and + pads
  at their ends.
- A drag previews the value above the thumb and sends one order on
  release; a thin ink arc shows the workers actually assigned.

commits.subject: Add a thumb brush rail, one-finger pan and undo for painting (#473)
commits.body:
Zone painting cycled brush size, zone and Paint/Erase through repeated
taps on a bottom bar, could not move the map with one finger, and had
no way to take back a mis-aimed stroke. The phone editor opened its
brush chooser at the top of the screen.

- A brush rail on the thumb edge holds the eight brush masks as
  detents (smallest lowest); touching one magnifies it beside the rail
  and the thumb can scrub along it. Paint/Erase sits at its foot and a
  Pan toggle at its head. The toolbar holds Forbidden, Guard, Clear
  and Done, with Done under the thumb. It mirrors with the Thumb side
  setting and folds into two columns on short screens.
- A stroke held in the band along a map edge pans, as placement does,
  and keeps painting under the still finger.
- For six seconds after a stroke lands an Undo chip reverts exactly
  the cells that stroke changed in the player's displayed zones, with
  inverse zone orders sent after the stroke's own. A new
  OrderAlterArea constructor takes an explicit mask; the wire format
  is unchanged and round-trips in the area-order test. The harness
  executes a stroke and its undo on the real game and checks the
  authoritative zones return to their prior state.
- The phone editor uses the same rail in place of its popup chooser.
  Zone, script-area and no-growth strokes can be undone by restoring
  the covered tiles and zone bits; terrain, resource and delete strokes
  remove things and offer no Undo. The editor does not edge-pan while
  painting because its strokes replay in screen coordinates.

commits.subject: Drag flags by touch instead of panning the map under them (#483)
commits.body:
* Drag flags by touch instead of panning the map under them

On touch, a one-finger drag always panned the camera, and tap selection
cleared the held state the mouse uses to drag a flag, so flags could not
be moved on a phone at all.

A contact that lands on one of the player's flags, or within the same
24-point reach that selects flags on the phone HUD, now carries the flag.
Below the tap threshold it is still a tap and selects. Past it the flag
follows the finger at the offset it was grabbed, pans the map at a world
edge, and lands with one dropped move order on release, the same order a
mouse drag sends. A second finger, focus loss or rotation returns the
flag and ignores the rest of the touch. Spectators and replays only pan.

The flag lookup and move-order queueing move out of the mouse handlers
into GameGUI::flagAt and GameGUI::queueFlagMove, unchanged for desktop.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Size the flag reach for one-handed thumbs: 30 points, 36 at edges

The forgiving zone around flags, used for both tap selection and touch
grabs, was a 24-point radius: a circle of about 7.6 mm, the platform
minimum for a tap target. One-handed thumb taps stop improving at about
9.6 mm targets (Parhi, Karlson and Bederson, 2006), so the reach is now
30 points, about 9.5 mm across. Thumbs are least accurate near the
screen's edges and corners (Hoober), so within 96 points of an edge the
reach grows linearly to 36 points.

Points are already the platform's density-independent unit, so the
physical size is the same on every phone. The constants live in
InGameTouchTheme.h.

commits.subject: Give each game its own synchronized random stream (#522)
commits.body:
The synchronized RNG was a thread_local default engine, so a game simulated on
any thread other than the one that seeded or loaded it silently diverged. This
is the first step toward running the simulation on its own thread.

- Game owns MersenneTwister syncRandom, saved and restored with the game.
  syncStep, executeOrder, load and save bind it with SyncRandScope; seeding in
  setGameHeader applies to it directly. Game::bindRandom() binds it for other
  code that advances a game.
- During an engine session, a synchronized draw without a bound stream is a
  determinism bug: it is counted, and GLOB2_SYNC_RAND_STRICT=1 aborts on it.
- setSyncRandSeed and the RNG state helpers act on the bound stream, else the
  thread default. Map generation and tools keep using the default.
- The menu colony's game owns its stream instead of swapping it into the
  global engine.
- Particle effects use GameGUI::effectsRandom instead of C rand(); visual
  randomness never touches the synchronized stream (documented rule).
- test/check_sim_thread.py compares checksum sidecars, replay bytes and final
  saves between two executables over new games, a generated map, a v121 save
  and save continuation.
- Tests that build games directly bind the game stream (BoundGameRandom), and
  RNG continuity checks now inspect the game's stream instead of the global
  one, which they would otherwise pass vacuously. The guard-area golden is
  regenerated: its old values depended on draws leaked from earlier games in
  the same test case (master reproduces the new values when those earlier
  scenarios are skipped).

No simulation, save, replay or network format change.

commits.subject: Decouple rendering and the GUI from live simulation state (threaded renderer phase 0) (#534)
commits.body:
* Move per-view render state off Game and Map

Rendering kept mutable presentation state on simulation objects and in
function statics: Game::mapAnimationTime, the software terrain cache and the
overlay alpha buffer on Game, and static cloud and area-animation state in
the draw functions. On a separate simulation thread those would be shared
between the simulation and the renderer, and every view shared one cloud
field and animation phase.

- MapRenderState, owned by Game::ViewState, holds the animation phase, the
  area-marker phase, the cloud field, the software terrain cache and the
  overlay scratch buffer. Each view (game, menu colony, editor, torus
  without a GUI) animates independently.
- Map::identity() is renewed when a map is cleared or resized; the terrain
  cache follows it instead of Map/Game resetting a cache they owned.
- The building-gradient debug view no longer finishes lazy searches while
  drawing; it shows gradients as far as the simulation resolved them.
  (Unreachable in normal builds: Building::verbose is never set and
  DEBUG_RENDER_GRADIENTS is 0.)

No simulation change. Visual difference: the water/cloud phase restarts
when a game is loaded, and the menu colony no longer shares its cloud field
with the game.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add the lock-free triple buffer for handing Scenes to the render thread

SceneBuffer<T> passes whole values from one producer thread to one consumer
thread without either waiting: the producer builds into back() and publishes,
the consumer acquires the newest published value. pending() lets the
producer skip building while the consumer has not taken the last value.
Unit-tested for supersession and for torn or out-of-order values under
concurrent use; a ThreadSanitizer build of the concurrent case is clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Draw terrain, resources, fog and areas from an extracted SceneMap

First render passes moved to the Scene: SceneMap is an immutable copy of the
per-tile layers the renderer reads (terrain, resources, resource-growth
flags, discovery and fog for every team, the displayed team's areas), with
query functions identical to Map's. drawMap draws the scene published in
Game::ViewState::scene, or extracts its own when none is supplied, so every
existing caller (game, menu colony, editor, torus, tests) keeps working
serially. Terrain, water coverage, resources, fog of war and area overlays,
the software terrain cache and the GPU geometry caches now read the
SceneMap; the caches key on the source map's identity, stable across
extractions.

The layers are copied whole: 0.02-0.1 ms per extraction on desktop for
128x128 to 256x256 maps, at most once per drawn frame. No dirty tracking.

Software-renderer captures (3 late/early saves x 3 zooms x gui/map modes)
are byte-identical to the parent except one 16x13 region that already
differs between two runs of the parent binary.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Decouple GUI and simulation through client channels

Selection holds BuildingRef/UnitRef (gid plus scriptIdentity) resolved
through Game, so it can neither dangle nor follow a reused gid; the
Team::syncStep destroy callbacks into GameGUI are gone. New src/sim/
channels: ClientEvents (team GameEvents with a per-tick recent-event
pulse, order effects, building removal, unit conversion),
ClientCommandSink (script presentation commands, implemented by GameGUI)
and ClientRequests (latest-value client view and the SGSL Space
acknowledgement). Game::applyClientRequests switches failing-unit
recording to the observed building at the tick boundary instead of the
GUI toggling it on selection.

Simulation checksums, replays and saves match the parent revision
(check_sim_thread.py).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Hold the hovered unit as a UnitRef

Game::ViewState::mouseUnit was a raw Unit* written by the draw pass and read
by input, valid only until the unit died. It is now a UnitRef (gid plus
generation) resolved through Game::resolveUnit where input uses it, the same
model as the selection, so a stale hover can neither dangle nor follow a
reused gid. Drawing still records the hovered unit; with the Scene renderer
it will come from the scene's unit list.

commits.subject: Run the simulation on its own thread and draw everything from the Scene (threaded renderer phases 2–3) (#536)
commits.body:
* Extract the frame's Scene once per frame through extractScene

GameGUI::drawAll fills a GUI-owned Scene from the game through a single
entry point, extractScene(game, request, scene), and draws it via
ViewState::scene. Every part of the Scene is extracted there, next to the
code that draws it; callers without a GUI still let drawMap extract its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Draw units, buildings, effects, particles, the minimap and overlays from the Scene

The rest of the map renderer now reads the extracted Scene instead of live
simulation objects:

- SceneEntities: presentation copies of units, buildings and flags (field
  names follow Unit/Building, lookup by gid, team by index), per-sector
  bullets, explosions and death animations in drawing order, the selected
  building's map-view data (worker gids, failing-unit tallies) and the
  script highlight masks. SceneMap gains unit/building occupancy and the
  undermap layer, plus Map's display-coordinate helpers.
- Units, buildings, flags, off-screen worker arrows, path lines, bullets,
  explosions, death animations and building particles draw from it. The
  particle pass receives visible building gids instead of Building*.
- The minimap (desktop, touch HUD and peek, editor) draws from the drawn
  scene and keeps only the map size for input conversions.
- extractScene becomes SceneExtractor, which keeps frame-spanning state: the
  overlay map is computed during extraction and shared as an immutable
  snapshot, refreshed on a type/team change or per 25-tick window (windows
  start at ticks 25k+1, as before). The GUI no longer computes overlays.
- Docs: a Scene renderer section in docs/development/reference.md.

Software-renderer captures (3 saves x 3 zooms x gui/map) are byte-identical
to the parent except a 16x13 region that differs between two runs of the
parent too. New SceneExtract tests cover entity lookup, selection and the
overlay cadence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Draw selection panels, the HUD and statistics from the Scene

ScenePanels carries what the GUI panels show, extracted with the frame:
- SceneBuildingPanel / SceneUnitPanel: presentation copies of the selected
  building or unit (field names follow Building/Unit; owner as a value with
  its display name), including worker positions and inside-unit progress,
  and the answers to queries drawing used to make on live objects (repair
  cost, hard space for repair/upgrade, hunger, real armor, next level).
  Repair/upgrade queries run only where the panel offers them, as before.
- ScenePanelLocal and SceneHud: the local team's colour, prestige,
  conversions, max build level and site countdown; players, the wait notice,
  legacy script text and timer.
- A per-frame copy of the local team's TeamStats; GameGUI::teamStats points
  at it for the top bar and the statistics pages.

The desktop building, unit, resource, replay and choice panels, the top bar,
the overlay infos (selection circle, worker highlights, wait notice, script
text, voice indicators) and the touch inspector, dial and status views draw
from it. The buildingGuiState display accessors gain template versions for
presentation copies.

Touch input keeps validating against the live building: "is a building
inspected" follows the GUI selection immediately, held actions re-check the
live building before committing (healing cannot turn a held Repair into an
Upgrade), and the panel model is used only when it matches the current
selection. A touch test draws a frame before reading the action list.

Extraction tolerates empty player slots when naming teams.

SoftwareRenderBenchmark gains PROFILE_SELECT=building|flag|unit. Captures
with each selection on two saves are byte-identical to the parent commit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Draw building placement previews from the Scene

The building tool's preview decided room with Game::checkRoomForBuilding and
checkHardRoomForBuilding on the live map. It now reads the drawn Scene:
SceneMap::isHardSpaceForBuilding applies Map's rule (grass, no resource, no
building) and flags check the team's flags in the Scene. Placing a building
on click remains an input action against the game.

SoftwareRenderBenchmark gains PROFILE_TOOL=<building type>. Captures of five
tools on two saves at two zooms are byte-identical to the parent outside a
region that already varies between runs of the parent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Draw the torus view's selection markers from the Scene

The ring's building circle and worker markers read the live selected building
and its worker list while drawing; they now read the Scene like the flat view.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Make the voice recorder's thread flags atomic

The recording thread polls recordingNow and recordThreadRun while the main
thread sets them; ThreadSanitizer reported the unsynchronized access.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Run the simulation on its own thread

Interactive sessions now run ticks on a SimulationRunner thread while the main
thread handles input, GUI logic and drawing. There is no setting: the browser
build and hosts where thread creation fails step the same session serially,
which also stays the headless default and the equivalence reference.

- The simulation thread paces itself on the host clock (excluding time spent in
  the background), runs Engine::simulationStep, and extracts a Scene into the
  triple buffer only when the main thread has taken the previous one.
- Input, GameGUI::step, client events, selection checks and script highlights
  run in SimulationRunner::withGame, with the simulation parked between ticks.
- Drawing reads only the published Scene and GUI state. The drawn map size now
  reaches extraction through ClientRequests instead of a Map field.
- Pause, hard pause, running state and the CPU-load history are atomics; pause
  and local quit orders still take effect in the same tick.
- Simulation failures are captured and rethrown on the main thread into the
  existing abort path; suspension parks the simulation.
- GLOB2_SIM_THREAD=1 runs headless sessions threaded for check_sim_thread.py;
  GLOB2_SIM_THREAD=0 keeps a session serial for exact frame-count tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Cap threaded drawing by frame time instead of a fixed wait

The threaded loops waited 8 ms after every frame on top of vsync-paced
presentation, holding drawing near 45 fps. They now wait only for what is left
of an 8 ms frame, so drawing follows the display (about 100 fps measured
against 67 fps serial at a fast preset) and still stays below ~120 fps without
vsync.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
