commits.subject: Smooth unit motion setting, simulation-thread telemetry, ThreadSanitizer workflow and Scene boundary (threaded renderer phase 4) (#537)
commits.body:
* Record videoshots in threaded drawing

The threaded drawSession skipped the -vs videoshot capture and the match-frame
diagnostic that serial drawing does after each rendered frame. Both paths now
share saveVideoshot.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add an experimental Smooth unit motion graphics setting

With the simulation on its own thread, the screen redraws several times per
tick, but units held one pose per tick. The new setting (Advanced graphics,
off by default) draws them part of the way to their next tick: each frame
advances a unit's drawn delta by the elapsed fraction of the tick interval times
its per-tick step, stopping at the end of the current action. Position and the
32-frame animation follow the drawn delta.

- Scenes carry when their tick finished and the tick interval, and each unit's
  step speed; GameGUI::drawAll sets the frame's motion fraction.
- Motion is 0 when the setting is off, while paused and when the simulation
  runs uncapped, and drawing is then identical to drawing the ticked state.
- Presentation only: nothing reaches the simulation, saves or replays.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Keep drawing off live team state and test the Scene boundary

Terrain, resources, fog and overlay drawing still read the local team's
visibility mask from the live Team. They now take it from the Scene (or from
Team::teamNumberToMask, which defines it), and a build-system test rejects
live entity reads in drawing code and simulation includes in Scene headers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Extract the Scene before drawing overlays in MapRenderResizeHarness

The harness draws GameGUI::drawOverlayInfos directly. Since #536 the selection
markers come from the GUI's drawn Scene, which drawAll extracts first, so the
building selection drew nothing and the OpenGL case failed on Linux (the
harness skips without an 1800x1100 desktop, so it passed on macOS).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Adapt smooth unit motion and the Scene boundary test to SDL3

SDL3 removed SDL_GetTicks64 (SDL_GetTicks is 64-bit) and moved its headers
under SDL3/.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Report the simulation thread's performance telemetry

Collectors are thread-local. In threaded play the simulation thread's
collector was never reset, configured or exported, and the main thread never
captured its own draw and presentation measurements, so threaded sessions
reported little or nothing.

- The runner owns the simulation thread's collector (bindCollector), so it
  outlives the thread.
- Each client frame, with the simulation parked, the main thread absorbs that
  window into the session collector and configures and captures the session
  there, as advanceSession does in serial play; it absorbs once more after
  the thread stops.
- Records name the thread a scope ran on (main, simulation or both).
  Threaded sessions budget presentation against 60 Hz.

Serial and headless output is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Document the benchmark's selection and building-tool captures

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Run ThreadSanitizer on threaded games nightly and for threading changes

A separate workflow builds glob2 with ThreadSanitizer and runs a headless game
on the simulation thread and a windowed game under Xvfb, failing on any data
race. It runs nightly, on demand and on pull requests touching the code the
simulation and main threads share, so it does not add a sanitizer build to
every pull request. Thread leaks are not reported: SDL3 leaves its startup
threads unjoined at exit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Quote the ThreadSanitizer report step so the workflow parses

A plain YAML scalar cannot contain ': ', so GitHub rejected the workflow file.
Checked with PyYAML and actionlint.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Run the ThreadSanitizer windowed game without PulseAudio

The first CI run found no race in game code; the windowed game failed on a
report inside libpulse, between PulseAudio's uninstrumented mainloop thread
and audio startup. The step now uses SDL's dummy audio driver, as other CI
steps already do.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Defer CI on draft pull requests until they are ready for review (#606)
commits.body:
* Defer CI on draft pull requests until they are ready for review

Nearly every queued build was a draft PR, and every push to a draft ran the
full 49-job matrix (about 290 runner-minutes). Drafts now run only the change
selector and its contract suites: the selector selects no downstream checks
for a draft, so the aggregate gate passes with everything skipped. The build
workflow also runs on ready_for_review, which runs the selected checks for the
same commit. Master pushes, schedules and ready PRs are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Skip ThreadSanitizer on drafts and suppress SDL3_net's shutdown race

The workflow's first full run built everything, ran the headless threaded game
clean and played the windowed game to the end, then failed at process exit:
SDL3_net's NET_Quit (from atexit) destroys the resolver's mutex while an idle
resolver thread still waits on it. test/tsan.supp suppresses exactly that, with
the reason; game code is never suppressed. Draft PRs skip the workflow, like
build.yml.

commits.subject: Cancel superseded CI runs automatically (#581)
commits.body:
* Cancel superseded CI runs automatically

Every CI workflow now uses one concurrency rule: a newer revision of the
same pull request or non-default branch cancels the older run. Master runs
finish once started, while a newer pending master run still replaces an
older pending one. Release, publication and deployment workflows keep their
non-cancelling groups, and call-only reusable workflows declare none.

A lightweight cancel-superseded workflow covers what concurrency cannot:
runs of path-filtered workflows a newer push no longer triggers, and all
CI runs of a closed or merged pull request. Builds that were cancelled no
longer spend a runner on CI measurements. A contract test enforces the
rule for every workflow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Cancel superseded thread-sanitizer runs like the other CI workflows

Master added thread-sanitizer.yml (#537) with the pull-request-only cancel
expression; it now uses the standard one and is in the canceller's
allowlist, as test_ci_concurrency.py requires.

selection as pull requests, diffed from the commit of the last master build
that ran to completion, so merges whose pending runs were superseded are still
covered. The nightly schedule and manual dispatch keep the full matrix and

completed master build fall back to full CI.

commits.body:
* Add the platform workspace and its JSON protocol contracts

platform/ is an npm workspace (Node 22, TypeScript strict, ESLint,
Prettier, Vitest). packages/protocol defines every JSON document that
crosses a process boundary as TypeBox schemas: MatchSetup (convertible to
a GameHeader without the binary formats), sim versions, match tickets,
relay registration and reports, realtime envelopes and messages, REST
resources and engine-agent jobs. It exports a JSON Schema per name plus
valid and invalid fixtures and signed test tickets for C++ contract tests;
a test keeps the generated fixtures current.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

device credentials, refresh tokens, entitlements, rooms, matches,
ratings (including AI entities per sim version), queue tickets, maps,
relays, blobs and engine jobs; typed Kysely access checked column for

Multiplayer M0: LockstepSession interface, vendored JSON, WebSocket text mode and HttpFetch (#501)
commits.body:
* Drive the engine's order pump through a LockstepSession interface

The engine now holds a LockstepSession instead of a concrete NetEngine.
The interface covers exactly what EngineRun.cpp and MultiplayerGame use:
setLocalPlayer, addLocalOrder, pushOrder, orderReceived, advanceStep,
tickReady (NetEngine::allOrdersReceived), getWaitingOnMask,
matchCheckSums, retrieveOrder, clearTopOrders and flushAllOrders.
NetEngine implements it unchanged, so single player, replays and the
legacy YOG/LAN games behave as before. The legacy multiplayer setup now
configures its NetEngine (latency padding, router connection) before
installing it, which is where a turn-based session will plug in.

Engine tests cover the interface contract on NetEngine. Headless runs
(4-AI multi-threaded and 3-AI single-threaded --run-game, -test-games-nox)
and a replay playback produce byte-identical replays and per-tick
checksum sidecars before and after.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Vendor nlohmann/json 3.12.0 for platform JSON

The unmodified release single header (and json_fwd.hpp) lives under
third_party/nlohmann-json/include with its MIT licence. The include
directory joins INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES, which the native, browser and
mobile builds all share, so code includes <nlohmann/json.hpp> on every
target. Provenance and hashes are recorded in third_party/README.md,
attribution in docs/assets/source-attribution.md, and the licence ships
as data/json-license.txt (also copied into the macOS bundle).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add a WebSocket text-message mode to native and browser transports

A NetTransport is opened, or a listener accepts, in Binary mode (the
existing ordered byte stream for NetConnection framing) or in Text mode:
sendText/receiveText exchange whole UTF-8 text messages of up to 256 KiB
for JSON protocols. Each connection is one mode; a message of the other
kind closes it, as text messages do today. Binary behaviour is unchanged.

The native WSS probe and listener tests cover text echo (including empty,
fragmented and 200 KiB messages), binary rejection in text mode, invalid
UTF-8 and oversized text.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add HttpFetch, an asynchronous HTTPS client polled from the UI thread

src/online/HttpFetch.h starts GET/POST/PUT requests with headers, a body,
a whole-request timeout and a response size limit, and returns a handle
the caller polls (state(), response(), error(), cancel()), following the
ApplicationHost FileSelection/Persistence pattern. Natively a Beast
HTTP/1.1 client runs on the caller's thread, pumped by state() like
WssTransport; in the browser the request is an emscripten_fetch (linked
with -sFETCH=1). Plain http:// is limited to loopback hosts.

WssTransport's TLS context and server-verification setup moves to
src/net/TlsSetup.h unchanged, so HttpFetch trusts exactly what the
WebSocket transport trusts (SSL_CERT_FILE, platform trust on Apple,
mobile and Windows).

tests/transport/test_http_fetch.py drives the http-fetch-test harness
(built by transport-test) against local HTTP and HTTPS servers; unit
tests cover URL parsing and policy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Include SDL3's SDL_stdinc.h in LockstepSession.h

Master moved to SDL3 (#487), whose headers live under SDL3/.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.body:
* Document the relay-sequenced turn protocol

Binary messages, framing and versioning, tick assignment, the per-client
jitter buffer and delay controller, reconnect and grace, desync
arbitration and the match record format.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add the turn netcode core under src/net/turn

TurnMessages codecs in the reserved 0xA0-0xBF message range, the
TurnSequencer relay core, JitterBuffer and DelayController, the
client-side TurnSession over an abstract transport, and the versioned
MatchRecord. Nothing in the engine uses them yet.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Test the turn netcode with a fake clock and a simulated network

Unit tests for the codecs, TurnSequencer, the jitter buffer and delay
controller, TurnSession and MatchRecord; an in-process harness of 2-4
TurnSession clients against a TurnSequencer under latency, jitter, loss,
outages, a restart and desyncs; and a check that turn messages ride
NetConnection framing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Name the link list type so GCC can construct turn harness matches

GCC 11 and 13 rejected Match({{a}, {b}}) as ambiguous: the braced list can
also build a temporary Match (links {a}, AI seats {b}) for the move
constructor. Clang accepted it, so only the Linux and MinGW builds failed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Bound a harness client's lag by what its own link can hold in flight

The settled-match check allowed every client the same 4 ticks beyond its
buffer. A client on a lossy link can legitimately be further behind at the
instant of the check: a bundle that needed a 200 ms retransmission is still
in flight while the relay keeps issuing ticks. The MinGW run hit that case
(client 2: 120 ms, 3% loss; 10 > 9). The bound now adds a bundle interval and
the link's worst one-way delivery, so loss-free clients keep about the old
margin and lossy ones get exactly the retransmission they can be waiting on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Turn MatchSetup JSON into the GameHeader and define the sim version

MatchSetup (platform/packages/protocol is the source of truth) now has one
C++ reader shared by clients and the verifier. It checks the JSON Schema
rules and then the cross-field rules, reporting the stage and a JSON
pointer, finds the map whose decompressed bytes hash to map.hash, and
builds the GameHeader: every human seat P_IP on every client, AI seats by
their CLI ids, ally team = alliance + 1, rules through the setters of the
same names. GameHeader -> MatchSetup covers LAN hosts and uploaded saves;
for a save, the seats replace the saved player records.

SimVersion is VERSION_MINOR, NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION and a SHA-256 over the
simulation data files (Maxima strategies, Nicowar tables, USL runtime),
with CR LF normalised so Windows checkouts agree. A portable SHA-256 is
included because the browser build has no OpenSSL.

The contract test runs every MatchSetup and SimVersion fixture from the
protocol package, from a vendored copy until the platform workspace is on
this branch, and then checks the copy against the source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Run turn-protocol games in the engine

Engine::initTurnMatchTask starts a game from a validated MatchSetup, the
map file whose hash matches it, the local seat and a transport to the
relay, and installs a TurnSession behind LockstepSession through the new
TurnLockstepSession adapter. LAN and the online client call it.

The loop pumps the session every frame and paces turn games by
tickIntervalMicros(), rounded to milliseconds, even while paused. Its
budget advances only with executed ticks, so frames that wait for a
bundle poll quickly. While the interval is 0 it uses the replay
fast-forward preset and lifts the MAX_CATCHUP_MS cap. needsReload()
reloads the initial state in place and fast-forwards; a refused client
leaves; tearing the session down sends quit(). Turn games never take the
single-player desync dump: divergence arrives as a reload or a flag.

Single player, replays and the legacy YOG/LAN games keep NetEngine and
their exact behaviour: every change is gated on a turn session.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add --verify-match and --sim-version

--verify-match <record> --map <file> --out <dir> replays a relay match
record through the path live clients run: Engine::initTurnMatch with a
RecordTransport serving the record's turns as a relay would. Human seats
are P_IP, AI orders are computed locally, and a seat's quit order never
stops the run. It takes the checksum before every tick up to endTick and
compares every reported one: verified, diverged{seats} (at least one seat
matched) or unverifiable (none matched, nothing to compare, or another
sim version). It writes verdict.json, result.json in the --run-game
format (now shared through Headless::playersAndTeamsJson; human players
show "human"), checksums.txt, a standard match.replay and artifacts.json.
Exit code 0 for any verdict, 2 for a bad request, 3 for a failure.

--sim-version prints {versionMinor, netProtocol, dataHash} for engine
agents to partition jobs by. --headless-catalog lists verify_match.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Test turn games with real engines and verify their records

TurnEngineHarness runs 2-4 Engine instances on one MatchSetup against a
TurnSequencer over the simulated network of TurnHarnessTest, now shared
through TurnTestSupport.h. AI seats run on every client; human seats are
bots that queue orders through the GUI's order queue. Each engine keeps
its own synchronized RNG stream, swapped in while it steps.

Every case requires all clients to agree on the checksum before every
tick, and --verify-match on the relay's record to reproduce them and the
live result.json team outcomes: latency, jitter and loss; a 5 s stall
with incremental resume; a restarted client fast-forwarding from tick 0;
a client executing a tampered order, repaired by an in-place reload and
named by the verifier; a player quitting through the sequenced order.
Forged turns verify as unverifiable and a lying seat as diverged. A
benchmark case measures rejoin fast-forward time against game length and
AI count.

test/fixtures/multiplayer holds a short recorded match and its expected
verification trace for the cross-platform checksum job; the golden case
regenerates both with --update-fixtures.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The native determinism lanes (Linux x2, Windows) now also run
--verify-match on test/fixtures/multiplayer/FourSquares1.g2mr, and a new
browser case verifies the same record in WebAssembly in Chromium, Firefox
and WebKit. The browser/native equivalence job requires all six per-tick
verification traces to be identical, and warns when they agree with each
other but not with the committed trace. Changes to the fixture select the
native, browser and comparison jobs.

docs/multiplayer/turn-protocol.md describes the engine integration, the
MatchSetup -> GameHeader rules, save sources and the sim version.

commits.body:

jitter buffer and delay controller, reconnect and grace, desync
arbitration and the match record format.

controller, TurnSession and MatchRecord; an in-process harness of 2-4
TurnSession clients against a TurnSequencer under latency, jitter, loss,
outages, a restart and desyncs; and a check that turn messages ride

* Vendor nlohmann/json 3.12.0 for platform JSON

The unmodified release single header (and json_fwd.hpp) lives under
third_party/nlohmann-json/include with its MIT licence. The include
directory joins INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES, which the native, browser and
mobile builds all share, so code includes <nlohmann/json.hpp> on every

* Add the glob2-relay role: ticket-checked turn relay over WebSocket

stream sources, OpenSSL and header-only Boost.Beast, and no SDL library.

  and with the same reasons as the platform's verifier; JWKS from a static
  file or the platform, cached, refreshed periodically and on unknown kid.

  tickets must agree on simVersion and humanSeats; ended matches leave a
  tombstone so a late ticket cannot restart them.

legacy message factory.

commits.body:
* Drive the engine's order pump through a LockstepSession interface

The engine now holds a LockstepSession instead of a concrete NetEngine.
The interface covers exactly what EngineRun.cpp and MultiplayerGame use:
setLocalPlayer, addLocalOrder, pushOrder, orderReceived, advanceStep,
tickReady (NetEngine::allOrdersReceived), getWaitingOnMask,
matchCheckSums, retrieveOrder, clearTopOrders and flushAllOrders.
NetEngine implements it unchanged, so single player, replays and the
legacy YOG/LAN games behave as before. The legacy multiplayer setup now
configures its NetEngine (latency padding, router connection) before
installing it, which is where a turn-based session will plug in.

Engine tests cover the interface contract on NetEngine. Headless runs
(4-AI multi-threaded and 3-AI single-threaded --run-game, -test-games-nox)
and a replay playback produce byte-identical replays and per-tick
checksum sidecars before and after.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Vendor nlohmann/json 3.12.0 for platform JSON

The unmodified release single header (and json_fwd.hpp) lives under
third_party/nlohmann-json/include with its MIT licence. The include
directory joins INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES, which the native, browser and
mobile builds all share, so code includes <nlohmann/json.hpp> on every
target. Provenance and hashes are recorded in third_party/README.md,
attribution in docs/assets/source-attribution.md, and the licence ships
as data/json-license.txt (also copied into the macOS bundle).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add a WebSocket text-message mode to native and browser transports

A NetTransport is opened, or a listener accepts, in Binary mode (the
existing ordered byte stream for NetConnection framing) or in Text mode:
sendText/receiveText exchange whole UTF-8 text messages of up to 256 KiB
for JSON protocols. Each connection is one mode; a message of the other
kind closes it, as text messages do today. Binary behaviour is unchanged.

The native WSS probe and listener tests cover text echo (including empty,
fragmented and 200 KiB messages), binary rejection in text mode, invalid
UTF-8 and oversized text.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add HttpFetch, an asynchronous HTTPS client polled from the UI thread

src/online/HttpFetch.h starts GET/POST/PUT requests with headers, a body,
a whole-request timeout and a response size limit, and returns a handle
the caller polls (state(), response(), error(), cancel()), following the
ApplicationHost FileSelection/Persistence pattern. Natively a Beast
HTTP/1.1 client runs on the caller's thread, pumped by state() like
WssTransport; in the browser the request is an emscripten_fetch (linked
with -sFETCH=1). Plain http:// is limited to loopback hosts.

WssTransport's TLS context and server-verification setup moves to
src/net/TlsSetup.h unchanged, so HttpFetch trusts exactly what the
WebSocket transport trusts (SSL_CERT_FILE, platform trust on Apple,
mobile and Windows).

tests/transport/test_http_fetch.py drives the http-fetch-test harness
(built by transport-test) against local HTTP and HTTPS servers; unit
tests cover URL parsing and policy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add PATCH/DELETE to HttpFetch, ApplicationHost::openUrl and the /realtime route

The platform renames accounts with PATCH /api/v1/accounts/me, so HttpFetch
gains PATCH (and DELETE). ApplicationHost::openUrl opens an http(s) URL in
the system browser: SDL_OpenURL natively (desktop, Android, iOS) and
window.open in the browser, which only reliably succeeds inside a click.
NetEndpoint accepts the platform's /realtime WebSocket route.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add the online platform client: PlatformClient, instances, map cache, invite links

src/online/ gains the game's side of the platform (no screens yet):

- PlatformClient: one realtime WebSocket per instance (/realtime, JSON
  envelope with request/response correlation, timeouts and events), polled
  from the UI thread. It signs in with the stored refresh token, the guest
  device credential or a new guest, says session.hello with the access token,
  reconnects with exponential backoff and jitter, checks idle sockets with
  session.ping, refreshes the access token before expiry (one refresh at a
  time, rotated token stored first) and re-attaches it with
  session.authenticate, and runs the browser handoff sign-in, resuming it on
  a new socket. Authenticated REST calls retry once after a refresh.
- InstanceConfig: the selected instance (official origin by default, one
  constant), per-instance device credential, refresh token and trust, in
  online/instances.json through FileManager and browser persistence.
- MapCache: maps by SHA-256 of their decompressed bytes, downloaded from
  /api/v1/blobs/maps/<hash> (isolated in MapCache::blobPath), verified and
  evicted least recently used beyond a size cap.
- Invite links (glob2://join?..., https://<instance>/j/<code>, --join,
  the web client's ?join=) become a pending join for the future hub. Links
  delivered while running arrive as SDL_DROPFILE (macOS, iOS), from
  Glob2Activity (Android) or the iOS universal-link continuation.
- Online::services()/pump(): the shared client, pumped every frame.

Unit tests cover the codec, timestamps, refresh scheduling, backoff,
SHA-256, origins and persistence, link parsing, the map cache and the client
against a scripted socket, HTTP and clock.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Register glob2:// invite links on every platform

Windows installer (HKCR\glob2 URL protocol), macOS and iOS
(CFBundleURLTypes), Linux desktop entry (x-scheme-handler/glob2, Exec %u)
for deb, rpm, Flatpak and Snap, and an Android intent filter. The official
instance's https://yog.globulation2.org/j/ links are an Android App Link and
an iOS associated domain; self-hosted instances use glob2://. The Android
activity becomes singleTask so a link opens the running game.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Test PlatformClient against the real platform API

platform-client-probe (built by transport-test) drives PlatformClient with
the native transport and HTTP. tests/online/test_platform_client.py runs the
platform API from a platform/ checkout on a fresh Postgres database behind a
local TLS proxy and checks guest creation, session.hello, request errors,
REST, a dropped connection, a scheduled token refresh, a browser sign-in
completed on the web page while the socket drops, a returning launch,
refresh-token reuse with device-credential fallback, and sign-out. Skipped
without GLOB2_PLATFORM_DIR and GLOB2_PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Document the online client

docs/multiplayer/client.md covers the PlatformClient API, connection,
sign-in and token rules, stored credentials and trust, the map cache,
invite links and their registration, and the tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

scons/official_instance.py holds the origin (https://glob2online.com) and the
official_instance= SCons argument overrides it. Desktop, web and mobile builds

Master moved to SDL3 (#487), whose headers live under SDL3/.

Master moved to SDL3 (#487): invite links dropped on the app arrive as

commits.subject: Engine-agent job runners, warm map pool and match history views (#506)
commits.body:
* Carry verifier team statistics and timelines in verify-match results

VerifiedTeam gains optional statistics (final team counters) and timeline
(the engine's 512-tick end-of-game samples), so the worker can store match
history without reading engine files. submitEngineJob accepts a caller-chosen
job id for callers that record it before submitting.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Run engine jobs with the glob2 headless binary

HeadlessEngineRunner replaces the unsupported default when ENGINE_BINARY is
set: generate-map (structured generator, checked against the catalog),
validate-map and render-preview (the game's map loader and PNG preview), and
verify-match (the --verify-match contract being built in M1). Each job runs in
its own scratch directory with a timeout, process-group kill, ulimit CPU,
file-size and (Linux) memory limits and a minimal environment; blobs are
content-addressed by the SHA-256 of decompressed bytes and registered in the
blobs table. The agent learns VERSION_MINOR and NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION from
--headless-catalog and the data hash from the binary when it can report it,
otherwise from ENGINE_DATA_HASH. On a job's last attempt, retried errors are
reported as internal failures.

Tests use a fake binary for every path and, with GLOB2_BINARY set, run
generate, validate and preview on default-pool generators with a real binary.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add the warm map pool and verified match history views

Migration 0004 adds warm_maps and aggregate views over verified matches of
the last 90 days: per-seat results, win rates by queue, map and generator,
game lengths, team timelines and a player's economy curve against their own
average. The worker leader keeps WARM_MAPS_PER_ENTRY pre-generated maps per
queue pool entry and served sim version, backing off failing entries;
takeWarmMap() hands one to a match starter. Verify results now store team
statistics and timelines in match_team_stats and link the record, replay and
result blobs in match_artifacts.

* Test the turn netcode with a fake clock and a simulated network

Unit tests for the codecs, TurnSequencer, the jitter buffer and delay
controller, TurnSession and MatchRecord; an in-process harness of 2-4
TurnSession clients against a TurnSequencer under latency, jitter, loss,
outages, a restart and desyncs; and a check that turn messages ride
NetConnection framing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Turn MatchSetup JSON into the GameHeader and define the sim version

MatchSetup (platform/packages/protocol is the source of truth) now has one
C++ reader shared by clients and the verifier. It checks the JSON Schema
rules and then the cross-field rules, reporting the stage and a JSON
pointer, finds the map whose decompressed bytes hash to map.hash, and
builds the GameHeader: every human seat P_IP on every client, AI seats by
their CLI ids, ally team = alliance + 1, rules through the setters of the
same names. GameHeader -> MatchSetup covers LAN hosts and uploaded saves;
for a save, the seats replace the saved player records.

SimVersion is VERSION_MINOR, NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION and a SHA-256 over the
simulation data files (Maxima strategies, Nicowar tables, USL runtime),
with CR LF normalised so Windows checkouts agree. A portable SHA-256 is
included because the browser build has no OpenSSL.

The contract test runs every MatchSetup and SimVersion fixture from the
protocol package, from a vendored copy until the platform workspace is on
this branch, and then checks the copy against the source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Run turn-protocol games in the engine

Engine::initTurnMatchTask starts a game from a validated MatchSetup, the
map file whose hash matches it, the local seat and a transport to the
relay, and installs a TurnSession behind LockstepSession through the new
TurnLockstepSession adapter. LAN and the online client call it.

The loop pumps the session every frame and paces turn games by
tickIntervalMicros(), rounded to milliseconds, even while paused. Its
budget advances only with executed ticks, so frames that wait for a
bundle poll quickly. While the interval is 0 it uses the replay
fast-forward preset and lifts the MAX_CATCHUP_MS cap. needsReload()
reloads the initial state in place and fast-forwards; a refused client
leaves; tearing the session down sends quit(). Turn games never take the
single-player desync dump: divergence arrives as a reload or a flag.

Single player, replays and the legacy YOG/LAN games keep NetEngine and
their exact behaviour: every change is gated on a turn session.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add --verify-match and --sim-version

--verify-match <record> --map <file> --out <dir> replays a relay match
record through the path live clients run: Engine::initTurnMatch with a
RecordTransport serving the record's turns as a relay would. Human seats
are P_IP, AI orders are computed locally, and a seat's quit order never
stops the run. It takes the checksum before every tick up to endTick and
compares every reported one: verified, diverged{seats} (at least one seat
matched) or unverifiable (none matched, nothing to compare, or another
sim version). It writes verdict.json, result.json in the --run-game
format (now shared through Headless::playersAndTeamsJson; human players
show "human"), checksums.txt, a standard match.replay and artifacts.json.
Exit code 0 for any verdict, 2 for a bad request, 3 for a failure.

--sim-version prints {versionMinor, netProtocol, dataHash} for engine
agents to partition jobs by. --headless-catalog lists verify_match.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Test turn games with real engines and verify their records

TurnEngineHarness runs 2-4 Engine instances on one MatchSetup against a
TurnSequencer over the simulated network of TurnHarnessTest, now shared
through TurnTestSupport.h. AI seats run on every client; human seats are
bots that queue orders through the GUI's order queue. Each engine keeps
its own synchronized RNG stream, swapped in while it steps.

Every case requires all clients to agree on the checksum before every
tick, and --verify-match on the relay's record to reproduce them and the
live result.json team outcomes: latency, jitter and loss; a 5 s stall
with incremental resume; a restarted client fast-forwarding from tick 0;
a client executing a tampered order, repaired by an in-place reload and
named by the verifier; a player quitting through the sequenced order.
Forged turns verify as unverifiable and a lying seat as diverged. A
benchmark case measures rejoin fast-forward time against game length and
AI count.

test/fixtures/multiplayer holds a short recorded match and its expected
verification trace for the cross-platform checksum job; the golden case
regenerates both with --update-fixtures.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Verify the committed match record on every platform in CI

The native determinism lanes (Linux x2, Windows) now also run
--verify-match on test/fixtures/multiplayer/FourSquares1.g2mr, and a new
browser case verifies the same record in WebAssembly in Chromium, Firefox
and WebKit. The browser/native equivalence job requires all six per-tick
verification traces to be identical, and warns when they agree with each
other but not with the committed trace. Changes to the fixture select the
native, browser and comparison jobs.

docs/multiplayer/turn-protocol.md describes the engine integration, the
MatchSetup -> GameHeader rules, save sources and the sim version.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Pace harness bots in real time and check the verifier's replay loads

A restarted bot queued an order per fast-forwarded tick, which the relay
rightly treats as flooding. The verifier's match.replay is now also read
back with ReplayReader.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Advertise verify_match and the sim version to job runners

An older binary given an unknown flag starts the GUI and never exits, so
engine agents probe only what --headless-catalog lists. The catalog now
lists the verify_match and sim_version commands and carries the build's
sim version. The --preview-map report gains map.format_version_minor, the
save-format version the file was written with, so the platform need not
parse map headers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Compare only the vendored protocol cases with their source

Other schemas may gain fixtures in the protocol package without making
the MatchSetup copy stale.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Check every human order of a turn game before it executes

The relay passes order bytes through unchanged, so one hostile order (for
example an OrderCreate for another team) stopped every client and the
verifier on an assert. TurnLockstepSession now runs OrderValidation on
each human seat's order using only the game state at that tick and the
bundle's seat; refused or undecodable orders execute as a NullOrder on
every client and in --verify-match alike. Per-seat counts are exposed by
orderAudit() and reported in result.json and verdict.json.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Ignore hostile orders where executors asserted or indexed out of range

Building lookups, creation, worker counts, area brushes, alliances, quits,
cancelConstruction, chat and map marks now ignore orders they used to
crash on; voice no longer dereferences a missing mixer and its backlog is
bounded; MessageOrder no longer reads past a 9-byte payload. Valid orders
take the same paths as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Only cancel construction of the local team's buildings from the keyboard

The U and R shortcuts sent OrderCancelConstruction for a selected building
of any team, cancelling an enemy's upgrade or repair.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Test order validation with hostile clients, forged records and fuzzing

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Name the link list type so GCC can construct turn harness matches

GCC 11 and 13 rejected Match({{a}, {b}}) as ambiguous: the braced list can
also build a temporary Match (links {a}, AI seats {b}) for the move
constructor. Clang accepted it, so only the Linux and MinGW builds failed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Bound a harness client's lag by what its own link can hold in flight

The settled-match check allowed every client the same 4 ticks beyond its
buffer. A client on a lossy link can legitimately be further behind at the
instant of the check: a bundle that needed a 200 ms retransmission is still
in flight while the relay keeps issuing ticks. The MinGW run hit that case
(client 2: 120 ms, 3% loss; 10 > 9). The bound now adds a bundle interval and
the link's worst one-way delivery, so loss-free clients keep about the old
margin and lossy ones get exactly the retransmission they can be waiting on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Include SDL3's SDL_stdinc.h in LockstepSession.h

Master moved to SDL3 (#487), whose headers live under SDL3/.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Port the turn-game engine code to SDL3

Master moved to SDL3 (#487): headers come from SDL3/, and --verify-match sets
its isolated profile through GAGCore::setProcessEnvironment for both profile
variables, as the other headless commands do since #554.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Rename the harness tick constant and re-record the committed match

TurnTestSupport.h's TICK clashed with TurnProtocolTest.cpp's own TICK; it is
now TICK_PERIOD. Master's format 127 / network 50 changed the sim version, so
the committed FourSquares1 record (sim version 125-49) was unverifiable; it is
re-recorded with --update-fixtures. Its verified checksum trace is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Reject building ids past the last team before decoding them

Master's lookupBuilding (#571) checks the decoded team, but GIDtoTeam itself
asserts on ids beyond MAX_COUNT * Team::MAX_COUNT, which a hostile order can
carry. The hostile-order test caught it after the merge.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Re-record the committed match for sim version 128-51

Master's save-format bump (#601, format 128 / network 51) made the
committed FourSquares1 record (127-50) unverifiable. Re-recorded with
--update-fixtures; its verified checksum trace is unchanged.

commits.subject: Show a draw, not a win, when non-allied teams tie at the top (#529)
commits.body:
* Show a draw, not a win, when non-allied teams tie at the top

When sudden death or the prestige goal ends a match with teams from
different alliances tied for the most prestige, every tied team is marked
as won, and each tied player saw "You have won". Classify the outcome
for presentation only: a team that won alongside a winner it is not
mutually allied with sees "Draw" without the victory animation, and live
spectators see "Draw" instead of "Match finished". Allies that win
together still see a win, and teams below the tie still lose.

The engine's hasWon/hasLost flags, campaign progression, multiplayer
result reporting, saves, replays and result files are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Let empty online seats never share a win on the end screen

Online rooms play empty and locked seats as AI::NONE colonies that stay alive
and idle, so a sudden-death buzzer at zero prestige marks them won next to the
real winner. classifyTeamOutcome and isGameDrawn now take the teams someone
plays (contestedTeamsMask: teams with a human or real AI player; every team when
none has one, as in a replay), and those idle colonies never turn a win into a
draw. Two players tied across alliances still draw. This matches how the
platform records the same match.

Presentation only: the engine's hasWon/hasLost flags, saves, replays and
result files are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Platform integration: self-hosted stack, room kicks, lost-relay sweep, map catalog and gated image publishing (#513)
commits.body:
* Move the YOG deployment to compose.legacy.yaml

The lobby/router stack moves unchanged to deploy/compose.legacy.yaml and
Caddyfile.legacy so deploy/compose.yaml can become the platform stack. Its
Compose project name stays "glob2", so existing deployments keep their
volumes; the deployment regression test follows the file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add the self-hosted platform stack and hosting guide

deploy/compose.yaml now runs the online platform: Caddy, Postgres 16, a
one-shot init (first signing key, relay key, migrations), platform-api,
platform-worker, engine-agent and relay, with replicas for the API, agents
and relays. Every service keeps the read-only, no-capability,
no-new-privileges hardening and health checks of the YOG deployment.

The Dockerfile becomes multi-stage: one C++ dependency stage builds
glob2-relay, the headless engine with its data, and the legacy servers; one
npm install builds the web app and the production platform tree. Engine
agent images carry their sim version (deploy/sim_version.py, the engine's
data hash algorithm) and can be built from an older source tree.

Relays register wss://<origin>/relay/<container id>; Caddy routes that path
to the container by name, so scaling needs no per-replica settings.
/internal and health endpoints are never served publicly.

tests/deployment/platform_stack_smoke.py brings the stack up and checks
it end to end; CI runs it on deploy, relay, migration and dependency
changes. docs/hosting/README.md covers setup, providers, keys, scaling,
backups and upgrades; server-image.yml publishes the new images.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Wire the stack to the rooms API: /j, relay keys, backend JWKS

Invite pages /j/<code> are rendered by platform-api, so Caddy routes them
there. Relays fetch ticket keys from platform-api on the backend network
rather than the public jwksUrl their registration returns, and the API reads
the generated relay key through RELAY_KEYS_FILE (the worker does not need
it). Private paths now sit in their own handle block, which runs before the
web app's catch-all. The smoke test asserts real relay registration and the
API's invite page; the hosting guide documents upload/record limits and
relay key rotation with RELAY_KEYS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fill ValidateMapResult.players for saves from the map report

The engine agent reads map.controllers from the --preview-map report and
lists each non-empty slot's team, kind (AI types are P_AI and above) and
stored name. Engines whose report has no names (before
multiplayer/map-report-players) get slot-numbered names, so older agents
keep working.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Data model for room kicks and the map catalog (migrations 0006, 0007)

0006 adds room_kicks (a kicked player's per-room ban). 0007 extends the
maps tables of 0001 for the catalog: how a map was made, like counts,
the latest valid version, moderation fields, per-version sim version,
engine jobs, preview state and notes, one open report per reporter,
de-duplicated download counting, and an index for plays by map hash.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Let room hosts kick players for ten minutes

room.kick {roomId, accountId} (host only, open rooms) removes the member,
opens their seat, sends them room.closed {reason: kicked} and records a
per-room ban in room_kicks. room.join answers forbidden with
details.until while the ban lasts; the room sweep deletes expired bans.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Abort running matches their relay stopped reporting

Heartbeats now record relay_seen_at for each listed match. Every 30 s
the scheduler ends running matches not listed for 180 s (relay dead, or
restarted without them) with end reason aborted, no verification and no
rating change, reopens their rooms and notifies participants
(MatchSummary gains endReason). A late end report from a relay that was
alive after all replaces the abort.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Format the save-players and lost-relay changes with Prettier

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add the map catalog backend (M7)

REST under /api/v1/maps: create a map, upload versions (validate-map and
render-preview jobs, reused for bytes already checked), list public,
own or by-owner maps with team, size, made-with and title filters and
four sort orders, map detail with versions and viewer state, edit and
delete, version files and previews, likes and reports. Moderators list
and resolve reports and hide or unhide maps (audited); administrators
may delete any map.

Visibility: public maps are listed; unlisted (the default) are reachable
by id; private only by the owner; hidden only by owner and moderators.
The same rules govern files, previews and blobs by hash. Rooms choose a
catalog version by hash only when it is valid, visible to the host and
loadable by the room's engine. Plays are counted when a match's end
report is applied; downloads once per downloader and day.

The worker applies validation and preview results to versions and keeps
each map's latest valid version. Protocol: MapVersionInfo facts become
optional until validation; new MapDetail, UpdateMapRequest,
MapLikeResult, MapReportReceipt/Info/List, ResolveMapReportRequest and
MapHideRequest schemas with fixtures.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Cover the platform stack in the CI policy and aggregate gate tests

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Serve the packaged web client cross-origin isolated on the platform stack

The threaded WebAssembly client needs SharedArrayBuffer, so /play/ sends the
same COOP/COEP headers as the legacy stack, serves the gzip sidecars that
browser/package-static.py writes, and the default client directory is the
packaged build/browser-static.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Generate warm maps with one team per queue seat

The warm pool passed the catalog entry's generator parameters unchanged, so a
pooled map could carry a different team count than the queue's mode needs. It
now sets teams to the mode's seat count, as the on-demand path in
play/start.ts does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Give registered worker test accounts unique display names

Migration 0003 makes registered display names unique per instance, and the
kick and catalog tests reuse names across accounts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Bring the hosting guide and architecture table up to date

The hosting guide serves the packaged web client from build/browser-static
and notes that SDL2-era releases need their own Dockerfile for engine agents;
the worker row lists map jobs and the relay sweep.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Publish deployment images only after the whole set is verified

The image workflow pushed each target's release tags as soon as that target
built, with no runtime check, so a broken stack or a partial set could be
published under a release tag. It now smoke-tests the platform stack built from
the commit first, pushes every image under candidate-<commit> only, and adds
the release, sha- and simver- tags once every target has built for both
architectures.

windows.h defines near as an empty macro, so two touch-harness lambdas named

commits.subject: Land the multiplayer rebuild: new screens, LAN on turn netcode, security, reliability and netcode fixes (#516)
commits.body:
* Let players unlink a sign-in method, never the last one

DELETE /api/v1/accounts/me/identities/{provider} removes the account's
identities of that provider; a registered account keeps at least one way
to sign in (409 last_sign_in_method).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Send the map title and a rating preview with every match assignment

MatchAssignment gains mapTitle (catalog title, else the generator name)
and, for rated queue matches, ratingPreview {ladder, before, ifWon, ifLost,
provisional} computed with the same OpenSkill model and side rules the
verified update uses, without creating rating rows. match.updated now
carries the history summary (with mapTitle).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Deliver the last turn frames before a relay connection closes

Leaving a game queued the Quit (and a closed window's PlayerQuitsGameOrder)
on the WebSocket and destroyed the transport in the same frame, so the
frames were often never written and the relay held the seat for its
three-minute reconnect grace. A RelayTransport destroyed with frames still
queued now lingers until they are written (at most 3 s), pumped by
Online::pump(), and the shutdown screen waits for it before exiting.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fill the client summary's order validation and online relay context

Engine::turnNetworkSummary copies TurnLockstepSession::orderAudit() into
ClientNetworkSummary.order_validation for every human seat when the order
check is installed (identical on every client). glob2 --turn-client sets
networkKind "online" and the relay id and region from the assignment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add ClientNetworkSummary fixtures from a real engine summary

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Document the relay and platform network telemetry wiring

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Document the turn input delay: stages, buffer rules and before/after numbers

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Name the link list type so GCC can construct turn harness matches

GCC 11 and 13 rejected Match({{a}, {b}}) as ambiguous: the braced list can
also build a temporary Match (links {a}, AI seats {b}) for the move
constructor. Clang accepted it, so only the Linux and MinGW builds failed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* End a decided match when nobody is connected instead of waiting out grace

Once a client has left with Quit(GameFinished), the relay ends the match as
soon as no human seat is connected, lagging or resyncing; seats still in
reconnect grace are marked left then. Clients send GameFinished only when
the game is decided (end condition, or this colony won), not when their
colony lost while others play on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Say where an online result is instead of spinning on Verifying

The results card shows waiting for the other players to leave (the match
still runs on the relay), recording or verifying (it ended), then the
settled result, and says when either takes longer than expected. While it
is open it re-reads GET /api/v1/matches/{id} every 10 s, so a missed
match.updated cannot leave it spinning. Quick matches get Rematch
(Online::requestRematch), which reads Join X's rematch after
match.rematchOffered.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Wire quick match, rematch, profile, maps, history and the leaderboard into the hub

The hub starts the shared quick-match search and opens QuickMatchScreen,
registers the match hand-off (an assigned quick match opens the starting
screen) and the rematch hand-off (match.rematch room, entered once the
match screens close), and attaches the match-found presenter. Recent
matches come from GET /api/v1/players/{id}/matches with live summaries
merged over them; Profile & history and Maps open their screens; a teaser
shows the top five of the first rated queue. The Room screen takes a
catalog map from Use in a room.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Enable Unlink in Settings > Online

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Report presence, game end and result phases in the online play harness

The harness logs the other seats' presence as the connection panel shows
it, the tick the game ended, and each change of the results card, waits
until the result settles, can leave by closing the window or by the
in-game Quit, and plays a casual quick match (quick role). Text keys for
the new strings; client and identity docs updated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Keep the result's status apart from apply()'s verification local

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Measure relay order deferral from the first unbroadcast tick

Since #527 the relay gives an order the earliest unbroadcast tick, so the
telemetry's baseline for a deferral is sentHorizon rather than the next
relay tick, and max_queued_ahead_ticks (next free tick minus the relay
tick) no longer underflows when that tick is not ahead of the clock. A
steady 15 ms link now holds no jitter buffer, which the harness expects.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Send relay bundles on their tick and flush client sends at once

The relay's match timer now wakes at TurnSequencer::nextBundleMicros()
(10 ms fallback for grace, arbitration and presence) instead of every
10 ms, so bundles leave on their tick boundary. Loopback arrival spread
around the tick clock: p50 8.9 ms before (bundle interval 2, loaded
machine), 1.0-3.1 ms after. Online::RelayTransport::flush() runs the WSS
link's I/O immediately, so an order is written without waiting for the
next poll. The relay test expects the new bundle interval of 1.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Leave a turn match with Quit, not the quit order, so finished games count as completed

The end-of-game dialog's Quit queued a PlayerQuitsGameOrder; the relay
sequenced it and closed the seat before the Quit(GameFinished) that

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Say goodbye to the relay on every way out of a turn match

- The local quit order is intercepted in TurnLockstepSession (onLocalQuit)
  rather than only on the exit flush: the normal order path submitted it
  first, so the relay closed the seat before Quit(GameFinished) arrived.
- Closing the window stops the screen stack without finishing the session;
  the engine's destructor now leaves the turn match too.
- After a Quit, the relay connection lingers (reading and dropping input)
  until the relay closes it: closing a socket with unread input resets it,
  and the reset could discard the Quit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Let a WebSocket reader that falls behind catch up instead of dropping it

The native transport failed the connection once 256 messages were unread:
about ten seconds of relay bundles at 25 per second, so a backgrounded phone
or a long reload reconnected. It now stops reading at 4096 messages or
1 MiB and lets TCP flow control hold the rest at the sender, resuming as
the game takes messages. The browser, which cannot pause a WebSocket,
queues up to 16384 messages within 4 MiB.

* Bound a harness client's lag by what its own link can hold in flight

The settled-match check allowed every client the same 4 ticks beyond its
buffer. A client on a lossy link can legitimately be further behind at the
instant of the check: a bundle that needed a 200 ms retransmission is still
in flight while the relay keeps issuing ticks. The MinGW run hit that case
(client 2: 120 ms, 3% loss; 10 > 9). The bound now adds a bundle interval and
the link's worst one-way delivery, so loss-free clients keep about the old
margin and lossy ones get exactly the retransmission they can be waiting on.

* Give each platform service a least-privilege database role; move the engine agent to an internal HTTP API

The API, worker and engine agent shared the Postgres superuser. The engine
agent runs the legacy C++ loader on uploaded maps, saves and records, so a
memory-safety bug there meant full database takeover.

- Roles: glob2_migrator owns the schema and runs migrations (ours and
  graphile-worker's) from init; glob2_api and glob2_worker get DML only, the
  worker without identities, device credentials or the audit log, and the
  audit log is append-only for the API. Grants are re-applied after every
  migration; graphile-worker's row-secured tables get a policy for the
  services. An existing superuser-owned database is handed to the migrator.
- The engine agent has no database role and no blob volume: it leases jobs,
  reports results and moves blobs through /internal/v1/engine on
  platform-api with a bearer agent key. Blob reads are limited to the hashes
  the leased job names. engine_jobs is the queue (migration 0010); results
  still reach the worker as a graphile job, enqueued in the same transaction
  as the report. A sweep fails jobs whose last lease ran out.
- init generates a password per role and the agent key into separate
  volumes; each service mounts only its own. POSTGRES_PASSWORD is blanked
  in the services' environment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Relay: agree on a finished game, drop floods, arbitrate incrementally, wake on demand

One client's Quit(GameFinished) no longer ends the match or cuts the others'
reconnect grace: a match is decided (and reported completed) only when every
human seat still playing at the first claim left with GameFinished too.

An order beyond the flood limit is dropped and counted instead of rejecting
the client, which used to throw the player out of the match.

Arbitration keeps the ticks still waiting for reports in their own set, so
update() and tellRejoin() no longer walk every report since tick 0, and the
relay's match timer sleeps until TurnSequencer::nextWakeMicros() (once per
tick while anyone is connected, about once a second when nobody is) instead
of waking every 10 ms.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Pace and coalesce turn orders on the client

TurnSession sends at most what the relay sequences (a burst of four, then one
order per tick) and keeps the rest in a bounded local queue where a later
order with the same target replaces a waiting one: flag moves (keeping the
drop), worker counts, flag ranges and other absolute settings, and the pause
state. Voice has its own small queue and goes out only when no gameplay order
waits. A Reject(Flooding) reconnects instead of ending the session, quitting
sends what is still queued, and tooManyActions() tells the HUD when orders back
up. Telemetry counts coalesced and dropped orders and the queue depth.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Limit pausing in queue matches, deterministically

MatchSetup gains an optional pauseLimit {pauses, seconds}; the platform sets
{3, 60} for every queue match, rooms and LAN stay unlimited. TurnLockstepSession
keeps the pause bookkeeping from the orders it executes, so every client and
the verifier agree: a pause beyond a seat's limit executes as a NullOrder
(stale, pause_limit), ticks paused count against the seat whose pause runs,
and the engine executes a PauseGameOrder(false) for it when its time is used
up. Any player may resume. Clients from before refuse a setup with the field.

The HUD says when a pause is refused, when a seat's pause time ran out, and
when too many actions are waiting to be sent.

* Share abuse limits across API replicas; lock out password guessing; bound uploads and sign-in attempts; add edge security headers

- Rate limits that matter whatever replica answers are sliding-window
  counters in Postgres (migration 0011, rate_limit_take, one round trip):
  sign-in routes per address and route, new guests, browser sign-in

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix kerned text gaps ("Tu torial") in SDL3_ttf builds without HarfBuzz

SDL3_ttf 3.2.2 (and its main branch) adds the FreeType kerning delta and the
lsb/rsb hinting correction to the current glyph's x_offset when it is built
without HarfBuzz, as all of our builds are. That moves one glyph without
moving the pen, so a negative pair pulls the second letter under the first
and leaves a gap before the next one: "Tu torial", "Yo u", "Wa rrush",
"To ols", "Te ams". SDL2_ttf moved the pen. Neither the font nor the browser
subset is involved: the original DejaVu font renders the same way, and the
gap disappears with kerning off.

- scons/vcpkg-ports/sdl3-ttf/kerning-moves-pen.patch adds the correction to
  the previous glyph's advance instead. sdl3_dependencies.py applies it (and
  records it in the prefix identity, so existing prefixes rebuild) and the
  vcpkg overlay lists it, which covers native, browser, Debian, Fedora, snap,
  Windows and mobile builds.
- TrueTypeFont opens every font through openFont(), which probes the linked
  library once (the pen width of "ToTo" with and without kerning) and turns
  kerning off where it would misplace glyphs, for system SDL3_ttf builds that
  lack the patch.
- FontKerningTest: the bundled library moves the pen; pair widths equal the
  glyph advances plus kerning; and no gap in "Tutorial", "You", "Warrush",
  "Tools", "Teams" is wider than the same word unkerned, at 13-32 px. Against
  the unpatched library the first case fails and the other two pass (the
  fallback). Build-system tests check the patch is wired and applies to the
  pinned archive.

commits.subject: M9 cutover 2/3: remove the legacy YOG lobby, server, router and IRC (#631)
commits.body:
* Remove the legacy YOG lobby, its server and router, and IRC

The new online platform (rooms, quick match, relay) and LAN on the turn
protocol replace YOG; this is the M9 cutover. Players start fresh: no YOG
account or data is imported.

Deleted: src/yog/ (121 files), src/net/irc/ and the browser IRC stub, the
legacy room screens (MultiplayerGame*, MultiplayerGameScreen,
SessionTabsScreen, YogRoom), LANGameInformation, NetGamePlayerManager,
NetReteamingInformation, NetTestSuite, ServerControl, and every YOG-only
net message (Auth, FileTransfer, GameCreate, GameHeader, GameJoin,
GameLaunch, GameTeam, Lobby, MapDatabase, MapUpload, Registration, Router,
RouterAdmin; NetPing/NetPingReply/NetSetLatencyMode). NetMessage now decodes
NetSendOrder (still type 44) and the turn range only; the 0xA0-0xCF
reservations are unchanged.

- Glob2.cpp: no -daemon/-router/-admin-router/-y; the server/router entry
  points and their GlobalContainer flags are gone.
- Engine: no initMultiplayer or `multiplayer` member. NetEngine keeps only
  the local single-player/replay queue: the router connection, order rate,
  latency padding and increaseLatencyAdjustment are removed. It still
  replays AdjustLatency orders, so old YOG replays play back unchanged.
- Online hub: the "Legacy server" footer link is removed.
- Settings: the YOG password is no longer read or written.
- Build: roles are client and relay. role=server/router and server=1 are
  rejected (server=0 is still accepted); SERVER_SOURCES and libgag_server
  are gone; src/yog and src/net/irc leave the include path. The
  YOG_SERVER_ONLY and GLOB2_ROUTER_ONLY guards are collapsed to the client
  branch. The unit tests' order-codec-only build of Order*.cpp now uses
  GLOB2_ORDER_CODEC_ONLY.
- Version.h: YOG_MIN_CLIENT_NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION is removed;
  NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 51 (part of the sim version).
- Tests and tools: YOG-only tests are removed (LocalTime,
  NetGamePlayerManager, the YOG handshake, login/session probes,
  map-database previews, the browser YOG spec, native-multiplayer-peer).
  NetConnectionHarness now exercises framing and limits with NetSendOrder
  and a local blob message. The UI presentation harness shows the LAN
  room in RoomScreen, and the menu/gallery harnesses drop the YOG screens.

No simulation code changes: single-player per-tick checksums, replays and
saves are byte-identical to master, and the sim version key is unchanged.

commits.subject: Share conditional-logit estimator and grouped cross-validation (#358)
Track room presence across API replicas (#633)
commits.body:
A member was marked disconnected when their last socket on one replica
closed, even while they held another socket on a second replica, and a
replica that crashed left its members connected forever. Each API replica
now registers in api_replicas, heartbeats, and records the accounts it holds
sockets of in realtime_presence (migration 0018). A member is marked
disconnected only when no live replica holds a socket of theirs; the others
expire a replica that stops heartbeating and re-evaluate its accounts, and a
replica whose own registration expired records its sockets again. Presence
changes of one account are serialised with an advisory lock.

commits.subject: Make the warm map pool a layer over generated_maps (#634)
commits.body:
warm_maps and generated_maps each submitted generate-map jobs, tracked job
ids, timed out and recorded results through separate code paths. A warm map
is now a generated map requested ahead of time: the pool calls the same
requestGeneration as rooms and on-demand queue starts, and applyMapJobResult
completes it; recordWarmMapResult is gone. warm_maps keeps only the pool
bookkeeping (queue, entry, descriptor hash, taken time and match), and
readiness, job, map hash and failure come from generated_maps (migration
0019). Untaken pool maps that are dropped take their generated map with them
so blobs stay collectable; a taken map keeps it, like any played map.

Also: one canonical-JSON helper, and the stale-job sweep uses the shared
engine-agent freshness constant.

commits.subject: Frame every u16-length stream with one reader and the relay's bundle splitter (#636)
commits.body:
Four copies of the u16-length framing (NetConnection, LanLink, the client's
RelayFrameReader and the relay's WebSocket read loop) become one header-only
NetFrame (encode, append, and a Reader with an optional unread-bytes limit
and in-place access). Each caller keeps its own policy: the same overflow
limits, and empty frames are still an error everywhere but the client's
relay stream. RecordTransport (--verify-match) now splits the record with
splitIntoBundles, as the relay splits resync bundles, instead of its own
copy without the 65535-entry bound. Bytes on the wire are unchanged.

src/relay/HttpClient.cpp (a Beast coroutine client on the relay's event loop)
each implemented resolution, connection, TLS, request, response limits and
deadlines. NetHttp::Request (src/net/HttpExchange.h, header-only) now does
that once on any executor; HttpFetch and Relay::HttpClient are front ends
that keep their own URL policy, trust setup, headers and API. The relay's
deadline now covers the whole request (resolution included) as HttpFetch's
does, instead of restarting at the TLS handshake.

commits.subject: Own the online services in the application and pass them to the online layer (#639)
commits.body:
Online::services() allocated the platform client, instance list and map
cache on first use and never freed them, so ~PlatformClient never ran, pump
hooks could not be removed, and the quick-match search was a second leaked
singleton. Online::Services is now an object the Application owns for the
run (ServicesOwner, its first member, so it outlives every screen) and
destroys at exit, closing the connection; it owns the quick-match search and
removable pump hooks. services() returns the owner's (tools and harnesses
without an Application keep process-lifetime services). OnlineMatch and
PlatformRoom take the map cache explicitly instead of reaching for the
global.

commits.subject: Let the LAN host's relay thread wait for work instead of polling every millisecond (#635)
commits.body:
* Let the LAN host's relay thread wait for work instead of polling every millisecond

The hosting LanHost's worker locked, serviced and slept 1 ms in a loop: about
1000 wake-ups a second for the whole room and match, on phones too. It now
blocks until a guest connection or the listener is ready (poll() on the
sockets the transports report through the new NetTransport::waitHandles),
the relay's next bundle or timer is due (TurnSequencer::nextWakeMicros),
another thread queued work for it (a NetWaker: the host's own player, room
actions), or 100 ms pass. Where transports cannot report readiness (Windows
completion ports, the browser), netWait() keeps the 1 ms pace.

commits.subject: Pack the unit sprites into sheets when packaging runtime assets (#229)
commits.body:
Sprite::load probed <name><i>.png and <name><i>r.png, plus a WebP
alternative, in every data directory until both were missing, so loading
data/gfx/unit opened its 2,816 frame files one by one. It now reads an
optional <name>.sheet index first, giving each sheet's layer, first
frame, frame count and tile size, and cuts the tiles out of the decoded
sheets. Without an index, or if a sheet does not match it, the sprite
loads frame by frame as before.

The repository keeps one file per frame, which tools/unit-animation
writes. tools/package_assets.py packs the frames of the sprites in
SPRITE_SHEETS (data/gfx/unit) into eleven sheets during optimized
exports, so every release package, the browser client and mobile builds
get them. Each tile is checked against its frame, and each sheet then
goes through the usual PNG/WebP selection. The audit lists the frames
behind each sheet so release installs remove per-frame copies left by
older installs, and the browser game package includes the sheets.

In the Linux export the unit set goes from 2,816 files (2.15 MB, 11.0 MiB
allocated) to 12 (1.66 MB, 1.6 MiB), and loading it with a warm cache
drops from about 195 ms to about 41 ms. Loaded pixels are identical to
the per-frame load.

Based on the design in #229 by Leo Wandersleb.

commits.subject: Fade the fog of war smoothly instead of switching it (#661)
commits.body:
* Fade the fog of war smoothly instead of switching it

The simulation swaps its fog buffers every 32 ticks, so every tile that left
sight during a window darkened on the same tick. A per-view FogFade now fades
each tile into the fog over about a second and out of it in 0.16 s, in game
time. The shade stacks the existing sprites at partial alpha, so it draws the
same in the software and OpenGL renderers and exactly as before when settled.
Enemy units, their bars, pips and selection circles fade with their tiles.

Rendering only: the simulation, saves, replays and SIM_REVISION are untouched.
The "Smooth fog of war" graphics setting (on by default) restores the old look.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Tidy the smooth fog fade after review

FogFade keeps the time it is drawn at and replaces MapRenderState's fogFading
and fogTime with active() and reset(). drawMap resets it while the fade is not
drawn, so turning the setting back on starts settled instead of fading through
changes it missed. The update loop moves out of the header, the shade layering
moves into a documented helper, the alpha curve's derivation is written out, and
units fade everything through one opacity. Tests cover gaps, resets, wrapping,
three-layer composition and a partially shaded square, and the harness restores
the zoom-detail setting it changes.

commits.body:

commits.subject: Repair Linux desktop packaging for SDL3 and the Amazon two-ABI APK (#699)
commits.body:
The v0.10.0.0 desktop publication failed in every Linux package:

- Linux archive: SConstruct handed pathlib paths to env.Install for the
  private SDL3 runtime, which SCons rejects ("'PosixPath' object has no
  attribute 'get_ninfo'").
- Distro source builds: the containers lacked make (Debian, Fedora,
  openSUSE) and SDL3's X11/Wayland build dependencies (XScrnSaver, XTest,
  Wayland, xkbcommon) plus libpng/libjpeg for SDL3_image.
- RPM: the same SDL3 dependencies, in the job and the spec's BuildRequires,
  plus git for the pinned SDL source patches.
- Snap: git for the SDL source patches, libxss-dev and libxtst-dev.
- Flatpak: pip tried to uninstall the GNOME runtime's own setuptools from the
  read-only /usr; install the build tools with --ignore-installed.

The Amazon APK packages arm64-v8a and armeabi-v7a, but #438's
abiFilters nativeBuild.arch dropped the 32-bit library, failing
"Package must contain exactly one main library". The Gradle project now
filters on every ABI android.py packaged.

commits.subject: Make online sign-in one click: no code to type (#716)
commits.body:
Signing in from the game used to take five or six steps: the browser opened
on a page asking for a code the game showed (with no way to copy it), then
asked the player to pick a provider again, ignoring the one picked in the game.

The browser now binds to the sign-in attempt as soon as it opens the link
when it comes from the game's own network (the IPv4 address or IPv6 /64 of
the game's socket, kept hashed on the attempt), and goes straight to the
provider chosen in the game. A browser on another network gets a single
"Yes, continue" page that shows the code to compare instead of asking for it

* Give colony skins the classic glob's glossy, bumped surface

Skinned units and swarms were lit with plain diffuse shading, so they
looked flat next to the classic sprites. The original Blender glob
material (datasrc/gfx/originals/units) bumps its normals with Stucci
noise at norfac 5 and adds a broad white highlight (specular 0.5,

normal through screen-space derivatives (no tangents in GSK1), with the
tilt bounded where UVs are stretched, plus a broad white Blinn term.

Put the team's stocked markets on the fetch gradients
commits.body:
Fetching a resource out of a market -- an inn pulling fruit a market of
its own team holds -- lived only in the block a worker ran after a
drop-off to pick its own next trip, comparing the walk to the nearest
fruit tile with the walk to a stocked market plus five tiles. Per-
delivery hiring removed that block, and neither the resource gradient
units walk nor the round-trip field hiring scores with ever knew a
market, so a freed worker could never be sent to one: market stock was
unreachable.

Make a stocked market a goal of the gradient itself. Every resource
gradient now has a "with markets" twin in which the tiles of the team's
alive markets holding the resource are seeded MARKET_DETOUR_TILES below
a tile of the resource -- the same five-tile detour as before, for the
resource having been carried there once already. A building that is not
a market fetches by that twin (Building::fetchesFromMarkets); markets
fetch for themselves by the plain one, so stock never circulates
between markets. The round-trip field a fetcher builds takes the market
tiles as goals with the same detour, so hiring, task swaps and the walk
all price a market like a tile of the resource and the nearer one wins.
On arrival next to a market the unit takes one unit of the resource at
its door and carries it home; the old take-at-the-door branch keyed on
ownExchangeBuilding is left as is, nothing sets it any more.

A twin is rebuilt together with its plain gradient, from the same
tiles in the same turn of the round robin, so the two never disagree
about the map; on its own only when a market's stock of the resource
appears or runs out (Building::addResourceIntoBuilding,
removeResourceFromBuilding, kill), so a unit walking to a market that
ran dry is redirected at the next step instead of arriving to nothing. Markets hold their stock in the
team's shared pool, so one change dirties every market at once.

Memory: one more Uint16 field per team, resource and swim class that a
non-market building fetches, allocated lazily like the plain ones.

The real-engine check in test/MarketFetchHarness.cpp runs one hiring
pass on a level-2 inn: stocked market and no cherries on the map -> the
worker is hired and the gradient's goal is the market; at the market's
door -> the take happens on arrival and the unit carries the cherry to
the inn; a cherry tile nearer than the market -> the tile is the goal;
the market runs dry -> after the rebuild it is no goal and nobody is
hired. Built with the market-fetch-test target and run in CI.

The twin is runtime state like its plain gradient and is saved with
the map runtime state (FILE_FORMAT_VERSION_MARKET_GRADIENTS, 98): a
resumed game walks the same field it left, which the savegame-safety
continuation check enforces. It sits in its own "markets" section: the
text format keys tiles by section name and the plain gradient's tiles
already use the numbered ones. Saves older than 98 load with no twin
and build one on first use.

Simulation behaviour changes, so VERSION_MINOR goes to 98 and replays
older than that are refused.

Fable 5.1 helped authoring this commit.

commits.subject: Verify market gradient continuation and preserve current routing boundaries
Keep market fetching independent of per-delivery hiring
Draft: market levels 2 and 3 store wheat and wood, then every resource
commits.body:
A market only ever held fruit. With stocked markets on the fetch
gradients, a market can serve as a depot for anything its level takes,
so give it two upgrades: level 2 stores wheat and wood next to the
fruit, level 3 every resource. The new types are appended after the
existing table (ids 51..54), so no saved building id changes; the
sprites are the level-1 ones until there is art.

A market's stock is the team's shared pool, so a level-1 market next to
a level-3 one would otherwise be seeded as a wood goal it cannot hand
out: a market is a goal for a resource only when its own level takes it.
The building panel lists a market's basic-resource stock like any store,
below the fruit exchange rows.

The market-fetch harness gains the level check: a level-1 market is no
wood goal, a level-3 market is.

Open for discussion: which resources level 2 should take ("wheat and
corn" in the request; wheat is corn in this code base, so wheat and wood
are taken here), the upgrade costs, and whether a market should also
hand resources to other teams' units the way it exchanges fruit.

Fable 5.1 helped authoring this commit.
