commits.subject: Rebuild colony-skin materials around a shared registry and add a catalogue (#819)
commits.body:
## What

Colony-skin materials get one source of truth and a real catalogue.

- **Registry**: `libgag/shaders/skin-materials.json` (ids, keys, names, picker groups, fur flag) and `libgag/shaders/skin-material.glsl` (the shading). `scons/skin_materials.py` compiles both into the generated `include/glob2/SkinMaterials.h` for the desktop, web and mobile builds; Colony Studio imports the GLSL raw; the protocol package mirrors the list (`skinMaterials.test.ts` pins it to the JSON); the API, baker, fixture tool and docs derive their limits from it. The hand-duplicated shader and its parity test are gone.
- **Shader structure**: each material fills a `SkinSurface` (albedo, perturbed normal, roughness, specular, metal, wrap, rim, cel, emissive, alpha); one `skinLight` lights them all. Meshes have no tangents, so normals are perturbed from UV-space height gradients (`skinTilt` / `SKIN_GRADIENT`).
- **Fur**: materials flagged `shells` draw `SKIN_MATERIAL_SHELLS` (8) extra passes pushed along the camera-space normal, in the tile renderer, the sprite baker, the studio preview and the swatch spheres. A cached per-map scan limits shell passes to quadrants that paint fur; the dead `hairy[]` flags in `ColonySkinPreview` are removed.
- **Reworked in place**: Classic glossy (soft bumped plastic, no longer crumpled up close), Matte (clay with fine grain), Metallic → **Riveted metal** (panels, recessed seams, rivet domes), Hairy → real shell fur.
- **New** (ids 4–21): Cartoon, Woven fabric, Oozy goo, Wood, Stone, Scales, Leather, Crystal, Lava, Chrome, Carbon fibre, Velvet, Honeycomb, Ice, Cloud (shells), Hammered metal, Candy, Slime.
- **Studio**: grouped swatch strips rendered from a single WebGL context (browsers drop contexts past ~16; the old one-context-per-canvas approach went blank once the pattern dialog opened), pattern dialog gets `<optgroup>`s.
- **Compatibility**: live clients shade ids beyond their catalogue as matte instead of rejecting the skin; the API and baker still reject ids ≥ count. No sim, save, replay, DB or protocol-schema change. Any shader edit changes `SKIN_RENDER_REVISION`, so **every published skin re-bakes** when this deploys (fur tiles cost 9 draws instead of 1 on llvmpipe).

## Feel

This changes how every already-published skin looks (ids 0–3 are reworked in place, as decided). Review images:

| | |
|---|---|
| Spheres, orange paint | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Globulation2/glob2/evidence/skin-material-catalogue/spheres-orange.png) |
| Spheres, blue paint | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Globulation2/glob2/evidence/skin-material-catalogue/spheres-blue.png) |
| Studio swatch picker | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Globulation2/glob2/evidence/skin-material-catalogue/studio-swatches.png) |
| Worker in the studio, all materials | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Globulation2/glob2/evidence/skin-material-catalogue/studio-worker-all-materials.png) |

Native baker tiles (128 px, exact `readSkinMesh` output, 4× nearest): [materials 0–10](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/evidence/skin-material-catalogue/native-contact-sheet-4x-materials-0-10.png), [materials 11–21](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/evidence/skin-material-catalogue/native-contact-sheet-4x-materials-11-21.png), [128 px sheet](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/evidence/skin-material-catalogue/native-contact-sheet-128px.png). Per-material studio captures under [`studio/`](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/evidence/skin-material-catalogue/studio).

At the in-game 32 px most texture is sub-pixel; the readable differences there are gloss, colour and silhouette (fur/cloud fuzz). The catalogue is meant to be judged zoomed in and in the studio — please play with it before merge.

## Tests

- `test/build_system/test_skin_materials.py`: registry ↔ GLSL ↔ protocol mirror ↔ docs ↔ `skin_render.py` inputs agree; shader stays GLSL 1.20/ES 3.00 portable.
- `SkinMesh/material contact sheet`: renders every material × {worker, warrior, explorer, swarm} through the baker path, asserts determinism, coverage, luminance bounds, ≥10/255 mean distance from matte and ≥4/255 from every other material, and pins `test/fixtures/skins/material-fingerprints.json` (±10 %; refresh with `GLOB2_UPDATE_SKIN_FINGERPRINTS=1`).
- `skins-materials.spec.ts`: fills the worker with each material in the studio, screenshots it, asserts each differs.
- The rotated-swarm determinism test keeps its ≤1-level tolerance for body materials and allows a bounded larger delta for fur (single-texel binary strands shift whole edges under sub-texel bilinear rounding; a cache/angle mix-up differs by thousands of pixels).

Verification evidence follows in a comment.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits.subject: Refine terrain boundary masks and tone seams (#844)
commits.body:
* Refine terrain boundary masks with traced sand contours, pebbles and rounder corners

Terrain boundaries still read as a chamfered 16-pixel staircase: local contours
were clamped to two pixels, every profile offered four shapes, single corners
were near-straight chamfers and diagonals a hard cross. This introduces catalog
version 3 and reworks the resolver while keeping version-1 sampling bit-exact:

- Profiles take four to sixty-four curves, and every curve is also read
  mirrored and negated, so a shared edge or patch picks from 4n shapes.
- `amplitude_q8` bounds local displacement per profile (up to four pixels).
  Local contours never leave their patch, so only the world-space warp consumes
  the eight-pixel halo; the shear window holds the full displacement over the
  central half of a patch, fold-free at that limit.
- Corner weights pass through a smoothstep, so corners approach quarter discs
  and lone quadrants become round blobs. `bridge_q8` joins one diagonal pair
  through a neck, chosen per vertex, instead of the four-way cross.
- `speckle_q8` scatters hashed pebbles of each material on a four-pixel world
  grid; they raise their material's score near an edge, producing detached
  specks and bites like the original sand art, and never touch interiors.
- The warp gains 32- and 8-pixel layers ([640, 256, 96]).
- `tools/terrain_profile_curves.py` traces the shipped sand curves from the
  original straight grass/sand transition tiles and seeds the fractured and
  cobblestone curves; the validator and its tests cover the new schema.

Presentation only: no simulation, save, replay or network data changes. The
gallery's 256-tick checksum trace is unchanged. The reviewed coverage digest
is updated for the intentional geometry change; the version-1 digest holds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Tone terrain seams with per-material contact shade and fringe

Boundaries were crisp but abrupt: ice simply stopped and grass started. A
cross-fade would average unrelated textures into a smear, so this follows the
original tiles instead, which darken a thin contact band (a lip on sand under
grass, a wet line on the shore) rather than blending.

- The resolver reports, per sample, the nearest other material and a Q8 pixel
  distance estimate derived from the score gap (12288 per pixel along an edge).
- Materials gain an optional version-3 `seam` object: a stacking `height`, a
  `cast_q8`/`cast_width_q8` shade applied to lower-ranked neighbors, and a
  `fringe` tint. Water ranks highest so sand and grass take a wet band at the
  waterline; ice casts a short shadow and a faint frost rim onto grass.
- The compositor tones only the dominant material's pixel within the band;
  textures are never blended across the seam.
- Ice feather widens from 0.75 to 1.25 px to remove one-pixel hardness.
- Validator, tool tests, a compositor test and the documentation cover the
  schema and the shading direction; the geometry digest follows the feather.

Presentation only; the gallery's simulation checksum trace is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Give every map a saved terrain look seed and an editor reroll (#845)
commits.body:
Terrain boundaries, pebbles, diagonal joins and texture variants were hashed
from wrapped coordinates and material keys alone, so two maps with the same
cells looked identical. Each map now carries a presentation-only terrain seed:

- `Map::terrainSeed()` is saved with the map (format 138, `terrainSeed` after
  the terrain registry) and shared through the map file; maps saved before
  format 138 load with seed 0. It is not part of `checkSum()` and no simulation
  code reads it. NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION moves to 58 because map snapshots carry
  the new field; the golden match record is regenerated for the new sim key
  and its verification trace is unchanged.
- Generators derive it from the generation request seed through
  `GenerationContext::deriveSeed(seed, "terrain-look")`, so regenerated maps
  are identical on every client without consuming the synchronized stream.
- `SceneMap` extracts it and `Compositor::describe` puts it in every `Recipe`;
  `PreparedCoverage` and variant selection salt every hash with a mixed form of
  it, and cached terrain pages record the seed they were composed with.
- The map editor menu gains **Reroll terrain look**, which draws a new seed
  and marks the map modified.

Tests cover reseeded variants and boundaries with intact partitions and shared
edges, recipe and page invalidation on reroll, save/load round trip and
checksum neutrality, generator determinism, and the editor action.

commits.subject: Add the terrain catalogue materials and procedural synthesis tooling (#852)
commits.body:
* Add procedural terrain material synthesis tooling

tools/artwork/material_tiles.py holds the sheet, perimeter-sharing, hashing
and style-statistics helpers shared by both material production methods.
tools/artwork/terrain_synth.py synthesises the twenty-four catalogue
materials from scratch (periodic value noise, fractal sums, domain warps,
Worley cells, scattered stamps and palette ramps), seeded per material,
variant and phase, with --check, --contact-sheet, --emit-catalog and --hd
modes. Existing tiles are only measured for style targets, never read into
outputs. Lava and ember field render four phases laid out as variant + 16 *
phase. tools/artwork/test_terrain_synth.py pins determinism, tileability,
perimeter agreement, alpha rules, style bands, colour separation and phase
continuity under the pinned Pillow 12.2.0 encoder interpreter.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Generate procedural frames and provenance for the terrain catalogue

Sixteen 32x32 variants for each of the twenty-four new materials (four
phases for lava and ember field, 480 frames in all) under
data/gfx/terrain-<name>N.png, written by tools/artwork/terrain_synth.py, plus
datasrc/gfx/<name>/provenance.json recording the recipe, generator hashes,
interpreter versions, statistics-only style references and runtime pixel
hashes. `terrain_synth.py --check` reproduces every frame byte for byte.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Register the catalogue materials, profiles and bindings in tileset.json

tools/terrain_profile_curves.py gains the rock, soft, crisp and brush
boundary profiles (seeded random walks with authored roughness, amplitude,
feather, speckle and bridge) and appends them on --write; existing profiles
are byte-identical. terrain_synth.py --write-catalog merges the twenty-four
material blocks (seam ranks, animation layout for lava and ember field),
their bindings and the pair treatments into the version-3 catalog.
tools/terrain_tileset.py derives required bindings from the five legacy
names plus tools/terrain_builtin_names.json and records per-material
provenance from datasrc/gfx/<name>/provenance.json in the compiled atlas;
its tests derive the frame count from the catalog with an 80-frame floor and
re-base the 64-material scalability fixture.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add the image-generator export and validation path for terrain materials

tools/artwork/export_material.py converts datasrc/gfx/<name>/material.png
(square, at least 512 px) into the sixteen perimeter-shared catalogue frames
through the shared material_tiles helpers and records image-generator
provenance: prompt, reference and source hashes, runtime pixel hashes and a
`replaces` record for the procedural provenance it supersedes.
--animate-glow applies the lava and ember-field recipes' procedural glow
ramp to the imported warm pixels for four deterministic phases (hybrid
provenance). MATERIAL_PROMPTS holds the shared header and bodies for
boulders, hedge, thicket, lava, ember_field, flower_meadow and outcrop.
tools/artwork/validate_material.py checks either production method:
provenance hashes, frame format, distinct variants, ordered joins, the
material's opacity rule and style band. test_export_material.py exercises
the path on a synthetic material in a temporary root. Procedural provenance
records are refreshed for the current generator hash.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Document terrain material production

Add a "Material production" section to docs/assets/terrain-materials.md
covering the procedural and image-generator methods, their tools and
provenance layout, the --check contract, the catalogue boundary profiles,
seam ranks, the translucent deep-water decision and the animated frame
layout; note the generated materials in source-attribution.md and point the
AI artwork README at the new tools.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Revise scree, marsh, boulders, lava, gravel and chasm recipes

Review of the contact sheet: scree showed an axis-aligned lattice, so it now
uses Worley cells under a per-cell rotated metric with no directional bevel;
marsh lost its vertical reed stripes for blotchy green-brown ground with
irregular rounded pools; boulders keep every stone inside the tile so no
stone repeats along shared edges; lava is thinner, dimmer and darker
(luma spread about 19 instead of 25) with a legible but muted preview;
gravel uses larger pebbles with per-pebble tone; chasm's streaks are thin,
diagonal and curved. Frames, provenance and the derived catalog colours are
regenerated; the other eighteen materials are byte-identical.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Pad the shipped catalog to 64 materials in the compositor fixtures

The catalogue ships 29 materials, so the fixtures that exercised a
64-material catalog now pad from the shipped count instead of assuming five.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Render a gallery of every catalogue terrain beside grass, sand and water

The TerrainValidation suite paints each catalogue type as an island with a
detached diagonal cell, plus deep and dark water meeting the ocean and lava and
a hole on the beach, and saves the composed frame as review evidence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Harden the material export and validation tooling

export_material.py refuses to export an animated recipe without
--animate-glow (and a static one with it), so the catalog's animation
frames never reference stale procedural frames, computes the glow masks
once, and records the platform. validate_material.py cross-checks the
provenance phase count against the recipe for every method, uses
GLOW_PHASES for hybrid exports and rejects procedural provenance on a
placeholder-only recipe. Tests accept image-generator and hybrid provenance
for placeholder-only recipes so the documented swap does not break the
suite, and cover the --animate-glow requirement. terrain_tileset.py's
docstring names the engine test that compares terrain_builtin_names.json
with its tables.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Rework material perimeters and revise recipes after art review

Perimeter quilting: the runtime blends the outer four native pixels of every
variant toward variant 0's reflected pixels, so the old shared border band
put the same frame on every tile. terrain_synth.py now keeps the perimeter
neutral instead (neutral_band: low-frequency luma flattened to the tile mean
over six native pixels, texture replaced by mean colour with grain over the
outer two) and keeps stamps three native pixels from the edge; the wrong
"no-op" comment and guide text are corrected. Confetti: scattered features
are now 2-3 native pixel soft blooms (flower meadow with darker centres,
embers with halos, loam flecks, meadow dots, snow sparkle). Recipes: ridge
rock and chasm use lit strata (chasm with floor channels, luma 40); scree
twelve to sixteen bevelled chips over dark dirt; mud specular pools; dirt
track paired ruts; hedge eight to ten clumps with gap network and bevel;
boulders two or three lit stones with cast shadows over gravel-toned ground;
loam umber; spring meadow desaturated at luma 105; deep snow darker with
blue shadows and a cool cast; deep and dark water tinted from the ocean
backdrop colour (alpha about 160 and 210) with soft highlight threads and
murk; void and chasm cast onto every neighbour (rank 8, 96/512); obstacle
casts and lava fringes stronger. Tooling: --hd no longer rewrites frames,
BUILTIN_ORDER is read from tools/terrain_builtin_names.json, provenance
records the platform and --check explains platform-bound mismatches. Frames,
provenance, catalog colours and seams are regenerated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Pin the catalogue boundary profiles and cross-check the validator's name list

The gallery's last row keeps its detached cells inside the rendered rows, a test
compares tools/terrain_builtin_names.json with the paintable names in the
terrain table, and the rock, soft, crisp and brush profiles get the same
geometry digest the shipped profiles have.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Drop the flat perimeter zone and converge tile edges onto texture

The gallery showed the mean-colour edge replacement as a lighter, flatter
frame around every tile. neutral_band now only pulls the very low
frequencies (radius-10 box blur) of the outer ten render pixels toward the
tile mean, tapering inward, and leaves grain, chips and colour variation in
place; stamps still keep clear of the edge. The render with the quietest
perimeter takes frame 0, since the runtime blends every other variant's
border toward it, and the style transform pools the statistics of all
sixteen variants so reordering does not shift a material's tone. The
contact sheet gains a 3x3 field of random variants at 1x and 2x after the
runtime border blend (translucent materials over the ocean colour), and a
test pins runtime_blend to tools/terrain_tileset.py seamless_sources on
committed frames. Deep snow's contrast target is 9 with softened anchors.
Frames, provenance and catalog colours are regenerated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Rebuild engine snapshots as the parallel foundation with chunk tracking and a shared executor (#857)
commits.body:
AI decisions read engine-owned immutable snapshot components and one engine
scheduler delivers every controller's ordered outputs at a match-wide delay of
0-8 ticks (default 0), executing in player order at fixed logical deadlines.
The snapshot is the foundation for parallelizing the rest of the engine.

The live Map and every snapshot expose one borrowed MapState::View with a single
inline implementation of each cell query; Map members forward to it. Map arrays
are change-tracked per 16x16 chunk and a reused pooled buffer copies only the
chunks changed since its last fill; GLOB2_SNAPSHOT_VERIFY=1 byte-compares every
capture with the live game. Published material planes sit in a dense registry,
teams keep sorted live entity lists, and component buffers are plain shared
pointers in a bounded pool with an acquire fence. ComputeExecutor hosts both
blocking map batches and deferred lane batches; AI decisions form one batch per
tick, joined by the simulation owner at the deadline, shared with workers only
when the measured work repays waking them. The separate AI worker pool is gone.

VERSION_MINOR 143, NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION 61, SIM_REVISION 27, replay floor 143;
golden match record, seeded-compositions trace, browser cross-replay fixture and
Studio digest regenerated. Paired timing against master: CPU 0.89-0.93 and
elapsed 0.87-0.95 across six scenarios; capture fell from 728M to 67M callgrind
instructions over 4096 ticks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Animate units from fitted rigs: blend shapes for workers and warriors, a bone rig for the explorer (#821)
commits.body:
* Add opt-in worker rig pipeline with shared deformation conformance

* Refine opt-in unit rigs and add reproducible performance diagnostics

* Document integrated material and five-clip rig validation

* Use current browser test DOM typings

* Account for fur shell passes in rig benchmark validation

* Fit unit rigs to the baked metaball clips

Replace the authored tube-and-sphere worker and warrior rigs with rigs fitted
to the baked GSK clips, which already carry the original metaball look. The
rest surface is the same limb-surface fit evaluated at the source rest pose,
bones sit on the original metaball chain with socket and segment-midpoint
bones, weights are solved against every baked frame of every clip, and
refinement moves bones only in translation and scale, bounded to one model
unit, with rotations kept on the chain so rig-rotated normals keep shading
the surface correctly.

Clips store 64, 128 or 256 samples depending on how their gait repeats across
directions; the warrior's swim stroke keeps every direction's own samples.
Worker swim and harvest join the candidate list, so all seven unit clips can
use rigs under GLOB2_SKIN_RIGS=1 / VITE_SKIN_RIGS=1. The explorer keeps its
metaball-bone generator in author_explorer_rig.py through the shared scene
helpers and regenerates byte-identically. install_rigs.py validates and
installs candidates and records them in the manifest; rig_silhouette.py
scores review captures. test_fit_rigs.py replaces the straight-shaft suites.

All candidates remain opt-in and unaccepted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Derive the worker rig's rest mesh from the un-posed baked frames

At the worker's source rest pose the body ball is smaller than its shoulder
and hip balls, so the rest surface there is an hourglass that skinning carried
into every frame as a crease across the middle of the torso. The worker's rest
mesh is now each vertex's mean over every baked frame, un-posed through its
home bone and symmetrised; the warrior keeps the source rest surface, whose
body ball is the largest and whose joints crack under the un-posed mean.
Worker walk drops from 0.50 to 0.47 RMS model units against the baked frames
and the torso reads as one body again. The fitter also gains torso-only
smoothing and rigid-torso options used to rule out the socket weights.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Let torso vertices follow the proximal limb bones

The fold across the middle of the worker's torso was not the rest mesh: in the
baked frames the torso surface slides outward over the shoulder and hip lobes
as the limbs move, and with torso vertices limited to the body and socket
bones the torso patch stayed compact while the limb rings covered the real
torso, leaving a fold at the boundary. Torso vertices may now also follow each
limb's first segment (--torso-bones, default proximal). Both models return to
the source rest surface; the un-posed mean rest stays as an experiment only.
Worker walk 0.47 RMS, torso continuous at every phase; warrior unchanged in
look.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Keep the bone-rig torso experiments as options

The seam across the worker's torso survives every weighting scheme tried:
socket or lobe attachment bones, torso influence sets, collar rings pinned to
the attachment, and geometric lobe weights. Cross-sections of the baked
frames show why: each limb's first rings swell into the shoulder or hip lobe
while the torso sheet retreats to a belly band, a per-frame re-solve a
fixed-weight skin cannot follow. The options stay in fit_unit_rigs.py for
comparison (defaults reproduce the installed rigs byte for byte); the
blend-shape path replaces bone skinning for workers and warriors next.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add GSB1 blend-shape clips for workers and warriors

Bone skinning cannot follow the baked metaball clips where limbs meet the
torso: each baked frame re-solves its surface so a limb's first rings swell
into the shoulder or hip lobe while the torso sheet retreats to a belly band,
and a fixed-weight skin leaves a seam where the two cross. GSB1 stores a mean
mesh, 32 int16 position shapes and 24 normal shapes per model (principal
components of all 768 baked frames) and 256 coefficient rows per clip. The
runtime blends, turns by the frame's heading, applies the clip camera and
feeds the baked per-pose upload path; Studio evaluates the same way.

fit_unit_shapes.py fits and reports (worker 0.05-0.07, warrior 0.11 model
units RMS against the baked frames; 99 % silhouette overlap through the
atlas; about 1 MB per clip against 15-18 MB baked). SkinShapeModel decodes
with the same bounds discipline as GSR1, SkinMesh adapts it beside rigs,
install_rigs.py records both formats, and workers and warriors select .gsb
under GLOB2_SKIN_RIGS=1 / VITE_SKIN_RIGS=1 while the explorer keeps its rig.
The shared analytic fixture, native and Studio decoder tests, a Blender
authoring suite and the asset contract cover the new format. The render
recipe tag moves to unit-rigs-v2. All candidates remain opt-in and unaccepted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Unwrap a conformal paint chart and track vertex correspondence

The v1 chart projected the whole body onto one plane, so sideways-facing
surfaces shared a few texels while the front compressed many, and checker
paint read as confetti. chart.py unwraps one symmetric quarter of the rest
surface with Blender's angle-based unwrapper as three islands (the torso
quarter and the two half limbs, cut at their socket rims, whose limb-side rim
vertices are duplicated and welded to the torso's) and mirrors it to the other
quarters, so front/back and top/bottom counterparts still share texels. Texel
density across triangles is near uniform (95th/5th percentile ratio 1.7 for
both models, against 5 and 8 before). The surface contract records the welds
and the validator checks the manifold and connectivity through them and that
seams stay closed in every pose.

The baked clips also re-solved their surface every frame, so paint swam across
the body and limb collars grew over the torso in overlapping layers. The
exporter now tracks correspondence: the symmetrised rest surface is carried by
one similarity transform per metaball component, blended by each vertex's
share of the field at rest, and snapped onto the posed implicit surface along
its gradient. Same surface, stable paint, no overlapping layers.

Every unit clip, sidecar, thumbnail, blend-shape clip and bone rig is
regenerated (worker 2898 and warrior 2514 vertices). The blend shapes now
reproduce the worker frames at 0.01 and the warrior at 0.08 model units RMS;
material fingerprints follow the new chart. Layout v2 paint does not line up
with v1 paint; all candidates remain opt-in and unaccepted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Enable fitted unit rigs by default and consolidate the pipeline

Workers and warriors animate from GSB1 blend-shape clips and the explorer from
its GSR1 bone rig; the baked GSK1 clips remain the fit targets, review
references and runtime fallback. GLOB2_SKIN_RIGS=0 selects the baked clips in
gameplay and the preview tools for comparison, and sprite publishing always
renders the rigs under the normal recipe digest. The Studio loads the fitted
assets without a build flag and falls back to the baked clip with a warning.

Remove the worker and warrior bone-rig fitter, its unselected .gsr candidates
and their manifest entries; accept the installed assets. Share the decoder
plumbing (bounded reader, camera checks, limits) between SkinModel and
SkinShapeModel, between the Studio rig and shape decoders, and between the
Python authoring, install and test scripts. Present every mesh format to the
Studio as a rest pose plus a pose evaluator. Rewrite the rig documentation
around the shipped formats.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Rework gravel, flower meadow and marsh after reference photographs (#900)
commits.body:
Gravel had no separate stones, flowers were too faint to read and marsh
pools showed the ocean through. The three recipes are rebuilt from
discrete objects after photographs of pebble beds, wildflower meadows and
tussock bogs: overlapping rounded pebbles with contact shadows, clustered

Discrete objects do not survive the runtime's mirrored border blend, so
materials can now declare "edges": "periodic": variants share one

commits.body:
Boulders, hedge, thicket, ridge rock and outcrop were flat textures inside
the terrain compositor, so they never stood up the way forest does. A
material can now carry a decor block: a sprite frame per cell, chosen by a
seeded coordinate hash (smaller edge frames for cells with an open
neighbour), drawn with the resources row by row so objects overhang
neighbouring cells and occlude each other. Both the cached GPU row path and
the ordinary path interleave decor and resources in painter order.

tools/artwork/terrain_decor.py synthesises the sprites in the game's soft
three-quarter view (objects rise from a base point with a lit top, a darker
front face and one ground shadow to the lower right), with HD frames and
provenance. The five obstacle grounds become quiet under-layers. The
editor palette shows decor over the ground.

Presentation only; the golden match trace is unchanged.

commits.body:
* Rename the sand foundation resource to silica

The glass-yielding foundation deposit shared its name with sand terrain,
which made editor palettes and docs ambiguous. Rename the resource key,
presentation name, sprite and source art to silica, and translate the new
[Silica] label in every language. Sand terrain is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add the editor brush catalogue, shared swatches and experiment gate

BrushCatalog is a pure model of every brush (terrain, resources, buildings,
flags, units, zones, areas, tools) with stable ids, actions, tooltips,
placement validity and experiment locks. BrushSwatches composes opaque
terrain and resource swatches through the map's material compositor and
ocean. MapEdit caches the catalogue, gates experiments on settings or the
map header, can enable an experiment for the map, and reports the active
brush id. Legacy resource selectors normalise to registry selectors, select
terrain <key> is added, imported names no longer hijack built-in actions,
and cancelling the terrain palette restores the previous brush.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Paint editor terrain cell-aligned with one previewed footprint

Every terrain and resource brush is now centred on the map cell under the
pointer; the +16px corner snap and the "on lines" preview are gone. Grass,
sand and water paint whole cells through the new editor-only
Map::paintLegacyCells, which resets authored identity only for the painted
cells, writes all four corners of each, and applies the sand-shore rule only
to corners outside the written set. Neighbouring catalogue cells (hedge,
lava, ice) therefore survive a classic stroke. setUMatPos and regenerateMap
are unchanged, so generators, scripts and the simulation are untouched.

The hover preview (desktop and phone) shows exactly the cells a stroke sets,
including the checkerboard gaps a corner terrain fills (BrushCoverage::
cornerClosure). After any stroke only the resources, units and buildings the
new terrain disallows are removed; the grass brush no longer deletes units,
buildings and every resource under it.

All terrain brushes offer Add/Del: Del reverts cells of the selected terrain
(for grass/sand/water, cells with any corner of it) to grass. Picking a brush
shape no longer silently selects grass. Resource previews mark cells where
the resource cannot go in red, and a stroke that places nothing shows
"<Resource> can only be placed on: <terrains>" in a status strip.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Keep editor save, load, share and quit decisions inside the editor

Window close no longer loses unsaved maps: a running top screen can veto
SDL_EVENT_QUIT (Screen::interceptsQuit), and the editor routes it, Cmd+Q
and Alt+F4 to the same in-editor prompt as Quit. Decisions are compact
EditorConfirmDialog cards over the live map (choice/<n> keys, safe
defaults): quit, load with unsaved changes, share an unsaved or
never-saved map (save first, then share), and reroll terrain look.

Fertility runs in an in-editor EditorProgressDialog sliced per frame,
replacing FertilityScreen; cancelling it during a save keeps the save
dialog open with a message. The fertility overlay is marked stale after
terrain strokes and offers a refresh chip.

LoadSaveDialog asks inline before saving over an existing file (except
the document's own file), and definition imports offer "From device…"
through the host file picker with a clear empty-folder message.

Teams, scenario and area-name dialogs mark the map modified only when
OK changes something; Teams cancel restores the map header. The editor
menu is grouped into File and Map sections with sentence-case labels,
without the palette entries. New "[no resource growth areas]" label and
"select no resource growth" action alias; "Unnamed area" without braces.

* Declare the editor dock and shared inspector interfaces

EditorDock (right-docked brush browser) and MapEditInspector (unit/building
inspector rows shared by the dock and the phone editor) headers, plus the
MapEdit WS-C block: hasDock/createDock/destroyDock/dockWidth. Editor uses of
menuWidth() now read dockWidth(). Implementations follow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Skip overwrite confirmation for a game's own save; update browser quit specs

Re-saving the save this session last wrote replaces it without asking;

in-editor quit/load cards (choice/<n> over MapEditorScreen) instead of
the former full-page MessageScreen.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Replace the editor sidebar and palettes with a docked brush browser

EditorDock is a right-docked, never-finishing InGameDialog built from the
brush catalogue: menu button, minimap (Minimap::setPlacement), icon tabs for
Terrain, Resources, Buildings, Flags & units and Teams, brush search, and
collapsible sections of labelled swatch cards with tooltips, selection,
locked cards and an Enable for this map action. The footer holds the brush
shape and Paint/Erase; areas, fertility, active team, building and unit
levels, the teams list and a stepper inspector for selected units and
buildings (MapEditInspector, shared with the phone editor later) live in
the dock. Its width is clamp(max(300pt, 20%), 240, 40%).

Pointer events inside the dock or owned by it go to the dock, keys only
while its search edits; map strokes keep their events. Brush and building
previews hide while the pointer is over the dock or a dialog; the map
status strip shows the pointer cell beside the zoom controls. The terrain
and resource palette dialogs are removed: their actions now switch the
dock tab, expand the group and scroll it to the top, keeping the brush.
Legacy sidebar widgets stay constructed for the phone tray but are not
drawn or hit-tested on desktop. Adds / and Ctrl+F (search) and E
(resources) bindings, the EditorDockLayout suite and gallery captures.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Choose the editor presentation live and build the phone tray from the catalogue

chooseEditorPresentation (MapEditPresentation.h) picks the phone tray when the
usable area cannot hold a 300-point dock beside a 480 x 480-point map, and the
dock otherwise, so touch tablets and touch laptops dock with touch-sized
targets while phones and small windows use the tray. GLOB2_MOBILE_UI and the
Compact/Spacious preference take part; unresolved hosts keep the legacy rule.
MapEdit::syncPresentation runs from construction and viewportResized, cancels
unfinished strokes and drags and keeps the brush, panel, team and levels.
MapEditorScreen's responsive viewport follows the editor.

PhoneEditor's tray is rebuilt from the brush catalogue by entry id: labelled
BrushSwatches cards with two-line names, group chips that follow the scroll
and jump on tap, every registry and imported resource, imported terrain,
group variants, areas, delete and a fertility toggle, and a Teams mode. Locked
cards enable their experiment for the map and say so in a toast above the
tray. The mouse wheel scrolls the tray or zooms the map under the pointer, and
mouse events are translated to logical pixels. The tray publishes its controls
for browser tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Refresh stale fertility from the phone tray and check decision cards on phones

The tray's fertility card offers a refresh while the overlay is out of date

commits.body:
* Draw resource and decor sprites in editor brush swatches

Atlased sprite frames report their position in the shared GPU sheet
through getTexX/getTexY. The plain drawSurface overloads used that
offset as the source origin within the frame's own CPU pixels, which
pointed past the image, so resource cards showed only their terrain
backdrop under the OpenGL renderer. Blit each frame's own pixels with
an explicit source rectangle.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Store terrain once per map vertex and derive cell rules from corners

Every vertex now holds a terrain ID (Map::vertexTerrain), the only stored
terrain state. Each cell's rules come from its four corners through
combineCornerRules: equal corners keep their profile, mixed corners make a
transition that is walkable when any corner is, never swimmable or buildable,
and otherwise as permissive as its weakest corner. Mixed grass/sand and
sand/water cells reproduce the retired shore profile exactly, so the two
shore types are gone and the catalogue IDs move down by two.

A per-map CellRuleTable compiles each corner combination once: properties,
movement costs per swim class, air costs and resource habitat. Map, snapshots,
gradient preparation, AI observations and JavaScript observations read rules
through it; pathfinding always uses the map's compact cost profiles.

Save format 144 stores the vertices. Older files convert at load: the
undermap gives the vertices, and a vertex touching a whole-cell terrain takes
it. SIM_REVISION is 30 and the replay floor 144; fixtures follow later.

Transitional adapters (setUMTerrain, setUMatPos, setCellTerrain, derived
sprite frames) keep generators, the editor and the renderer working until
they are ported to vertices.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Paint terrain brushes on vertices and lay beaches as a painting rule

Base-terrain brushes in the desktop and phone editors stamp the vertex
nearest the pointer, so the smallest figure paints a single vertex; resource
brushes still stamp cells. Map::paintVertices lays a sand beach where painted
grass or water would meet the other, and Map::layBeaches does the same for a
whole map regardless of scan order. Fix the live view binding to a stale
cell-rule array after a full rebuild.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Rework terrain paint tests for vertex brushes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Write generator terrain through the map's vertex API

Map generators, their shared toolkit and their tests no longer use the
transitional undermap adapters. Sketches are written with writeVertices
(formerly writeUndermap), vertex reads use vertexTerrainAt, square brushes
use paintVertexSquare, uniform maps use fillTerrain, and the in-place
controlSand pass gives way to the order-independent Map::layBeaches.

Code that used deferred setUMTerrain writes now builds a vertex buffer and
assigns it, or writes vertices inside an editTerrain batch: height-field
painting, Stone highlands, Watershed and Symmetric arena write whole
buffers; Shattered coast and Rugged archipelago, whose passes read their
own writes, batch setVertexTerrain. Road fords are collected along the
route and painted afterwards, so the route is still judged on the terrain
it was planned on. Tests paint a tile's four corners with a new
MapGeneration::paintTile helper in place of Map::setCellTerrain, and
compare and hash vertices instead of derived sprite frames.

layBeaches turns water beside grass into sand as well as grass beside
water, everywhere at once, so generated shorelines change; golden outputs
are expected to move. Map::controlSand stays in MapHomogen.cpp only for
the map image tool, which still calls it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Describe generator terrain in vertices rather than the undermap

Shared toolkit and generator comments now speak of terrain vertices and
tiles derived from their four corners, instead of the retired undermap,
Map::regenerateMap and Map::controlSand.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Stop decoding classic sprite frames in the renderer

Terrain is stored per vertex, so the renderer no longer needs to recover
corners from sprite frame numbers. Remove TerrainVisual::legacyCorners and
its tests, SceneMap::getTerrain (derived sprite frames) and getUMTerrain.
Every built-in terrain now needs a material binding, as the catalog parser
already requires for paintable types; classic grass, sand and water no
longer get an exemption through the compatibility table.

The minimap takes one sample per vertex, as map thumbnails do, instead of
the dominant corner of each cell.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Describe terrain cells by their four corner materials

A terrain Recipe held a 4x4 grid of half-cell samples, which since vertex
terrain is only the cell's 2x2 corner lattice repeated. Store the four
corners instead. PreparedCoverage expands them to the same nine patches as
before, so every pixel's coverage is unchanged: a standalone comparison of
the old 16-sample lattice against the new corners matched bit for bit over
all corner configurations and 3000 random recipes, sizes and seeds.

The coverage fingerprint tests enumerated a checkerboard sample layout that
no map can produce any more; they now enumerate corner recipes, with new
digests. Tests built from whole-cell samples use corner equivalents.

The overview takes custom saved colours per corner rather than from the
top-left half cell. Terrain pages compare only the vertices their tiles
read, and the per-tile revision allowance follows the corner count.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Import and export map images as one pixel per terrain vertex

Pixel (x,y) is now vertex (x,y), the top-left corner of cell (x,y). Export
writes each vertex's registered image colour, or the palette colour of a
resource on the cell it starts, plus colony markers. Import classifies each
pixel to the nearest palette entry and writes the vertices in one
assignVertexTerrain, replacing the separate undermap and whole-cell paths.

Seam repair and beaches still reshape only grass, sand and water; other
terrain keeps its vertices and counts as sand while repairing. Beaches use
Map::layBeaches, and seam edge reconciliation runs on vertices. Catalogue
types are recognised only by exact colour again: the check used the
pre-catalogue built-in count, which now includes boulders and hedge.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Read map reports and studies from terrain vertices

The report's underlying_terrain and the study's undermap counts now read
vertexTerrainAt directly, and the study lists every non-classic vertex type
in STUDY_TERRAIN. The report schema keeps the retired grass_sand_border and
sand_water_border keys as optional, since current reports no longer emit
them. The report harness paints single vertices, and its island fixture
keeps the two colonies apart with an all-water cell between them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Sample datasets and hazard benchmarks on terrain vertices

The dataset terrain channel takes the top-left vertex of each block instead
of the cell type, so a mixed cell no longer reads as unrepresentable. The
terrain hazard benchmark paints vertices: the safe-near-ice cell keeps a
mixed (hazardous) cell between it and the ice, the unreachable safe cell is
ringed by all-water cells, cache invalidation toggles one vertex, and the
custom-damage layout uses 8x8 vertex blocks so the corner combinations fit
the cell rule table.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Build the gradient benchmark against the current terrain tables

The standalone benchmark copied a fixed header list that no longer covered
the terrain tables' includes, and assumed a real registry of seven types.
Copy every top-level map and resource header, read TERRAIN_COUNT for the
real registry, and use synthetic registries of 32 and 64 identities, large
enough to repeat the real costs. The menu colony harness seeds resources on
uniform grass cells, and the generator scaffold writes vertices.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Describe vertex terrain and corner cell rules in the engine docs

The development reference now describes terrain stored per vertex, cell
rules combined from corners and compiled by CellRuleTable, MIXED_TERRAIN,
the vertex editing calls, beaches as a painting convention and the
conversion of older files, in place of the undermap, sprite frames and
shore types. The JavaScript tile docs describe corners, the material docs
the corner quadrants, the test guide vertex painting, and the replay notes
the 144 floor.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Describe vertex terrain in the map design docs and skill

Generator docs and the map design skill now speak of terrain vertices,
writeVertices and layBeaches instead of the undermap, writeUndermap and
controlSand. Grass against water is legal and beaches are a convention the
shipped maps keep. render_terrain.py draws tiles of other terrains (dump
codes 10 and up) in a neutral colour instead of failing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Port tests that painted whole cells to vertex terrain

Hazards, islands, corridors and brush strokes are now laid out on vertices:
one vertex reaches the four cells around it, walkable land always carries a
ring of walkable transition cells, and a crop cell never borders water.
Pinned counts drop the retired shore types, and the loader keeps a classic
cell ID that disagreed with its corners as whole-cell terrain.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Remove the transitional terrain adapters and sprite frame contracts

Terrain is written only through the vertex API now: setVertexTerrain,
assignVertexTerrain, fillTerrain, paintVertices, paintVertexSquare,
layBeaches and paintCell (the four corners of one cell). The undermap
adapters, setCellTerrain, setTerrain(sprite), getTerrain, controlSand,
makeHomogenMap, Tile::terrain, TerrainCompatibility.h and the saved sprite
frame ranges are gone. Saved registries keep only their colours; frame fields
in older files are accepted and ignored.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Regenerate simulation fixtures for vertex terrain

Checksum traces, the committed FourSquares1 match record, JavaScript and
Maxima checksum fixtures, and the linux-x86_64 generator goldens and
resource-epoch topology rows follow SIM_REVISION 30. macOS generator rows
were removed and must be re-measured there.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address review: stale docs and comments, dead transitional code, brush preview parity

- Docs: terrain type table, movement profiles, decor rule, script terrain IDs,
  the combine rule's OR-ed fields, two-sided layBeaches and the conversion of
  disagreeing classic IDs now describe the vertex model.
- Remove frozenCellRuleSnapshot, the rebuildResourceHabitats alias,
  BrushCoverage::cornerClosure and legacyClassicFrames; share classicTerrain.
- The desktop brush preview takes the same nearest-vertex lattice point as a
  click, so checkerboard figures keep the stroke's parity mid-stroke.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Widen terrain transition variety now that any two terrains share a cell

With terrain stored per vertex, grass meets water directly and catalogue
materials meet each other inside one cell, but most of those pairs fell back
to whichever profile was rougher, and the common profiles had few curves.

- Add shore (grass and fertile ground against water), liquid (water depths,
  wet ground against water) and organic (soft and fertile ground against
  grass, sand and each other) profiles, built from sine series with a weak
  fundamental so lone cells stay as round as before.
- Add 74 pair treatments (145 total), only where the choice differs from
  the default rule; boardwalks keep crisp plank edges, roads cobblestone.
- Extend contour sets: sand uses all 61 distinct traced edges of the
  original grass/sand tiles, rock and brush 48, soft 40, fractured 32,
  cobblestone and crisp 24, in their existing styles with the old curves
  kept first.
- Raise boundary_warp_q8 from [640, 256, 96] to [960, 352, 120] for broader
  meanders while the classic coast keeps its fringe.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Pin the catalogue fingerprints of the widened transitions

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Regenerate fixtures for SIM_REVISION 32 and describe vertex terrain as format 146

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix vertex test geometry for wrapped air routes, ecology and eager gradients

The air-route tests closed a two-cell-wide vertex barrier on an 8x8 torus,

commits.subject: Schedule building walking fields on workers by default, with greedy fetching and a strict executor (#944)
commits.body:
* Remove round-trip resource fetching

Workers always fetch greedily: they follow the resource gradient to the
nearest available source, then carry it back. This removes per-building
round-trip fields and their refresh and use stamps, their construction and
supplier seeding, round-trip candidate scoring in hiring, job swaps and
material choice, and the gradient.round_trip performance scope. Hiring
estimates, hunger checks, market eligibility and job swaps already ran on
the greedy path and are unchanged. Greedy fetching saved about 12% of
late-game CPU in #883's measurements.

Format 147 saves keep each walking field's last-use step without the
round-trip fields. Formats 95-146 still carry them; the loader reads and
discards them. LegacyRoundTripSave plays a format-143 save written by a
round-trip build onward. Replay, network and simulation version gates and
the regenerated traces follow at the end of this series.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Run deferred compute earliest due first; the owner never runs it

The executor's deferred batches now follow one contract. The owner submits
each batch tagged with the tick it is due. Workers run deferred jobs
earliest due first, in submission order within a lane, and claim a lane
job only after its predecessor completed. At a join the owner only waits:
it never claims or runs deferred work while any worker exists, including
when the only worker also runs presentation, which it interleaves with
simulation jobs. Only an executor with no workers runs deferred jobs on
the owner, at the join, because nothing else can.

Before this, joins ran the oldest live batch on the owner, so a building
or gradient join could execute AI decisions due several ticks later, and
owner time mixed work with waiting. Owner time now splits into owner work
and owner wait (compute_owner_jobs is zero with workers;
compute_join_wait_ns is the wait), which keeps each later parallelisation
legible. With one worker that also presents, a join can wait out one
presentation chunk; that is the accepted cost of the rule.

Placement::OwnerOnly is gone. Producers that opt out of sharing
(--compute-experiments without ai, --gradient-workers 0, a cheap AI batch
at delay zero) compute inline when they submit, outside the executor, and
still publish at their deadline. The lane wait inside execute() is
unreachable and removed with compute_lane_wait_ns. Gradient pipelines pass
due keys so periodic joins order against AI deadlines within a tick.

Joins cannot deadlock: workers claim only ready lane jobs, jobs and
presentation chunks never wait on the owner, and the presentation worker
returns to simulation jobs after each chunk. A harness case holds the only
worker in a presentation chunk while lane and free batches queue behind it
and checks that the join completes after the chunk, in due order, with no
owner jobs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add building field statistics and the fitted depth model

--telemetry gradient-stats (GLOB2_GRADIENT_STATS=1) gives the map a
diagnostic BuildingGradientStats. It writes one gradient-stats.csv row per
building walking-field lifetime (rebuild reason, settled depth, popped
entries per 80-cost band, resolve calls, and the O(1) owner inputs at the
lifetime's start), keeps a change journal of topology-generation bumps for
a shadow scoped-invalidation verdict, and adds a building_gradient object
to result.json. It only reads simulation state; with it off every hook is
a null-pointer test. The gradient.propagation.area and .resource scopes
split periodic propagation.

A gradient_depth tournament samples games across map sizes, formats, AIs
and generators with the statistics on. tools/gradient_depth_fit.py turns
the rows into a dataset, screens keys by held-out owner saving at a field
CPU budget, and fits a quantile table, emitted as the generated
src/map/gradient/BuildingGradientDepthPolicy.h with p80, p90 and p95
operating points. The table, fitted on 69 greedy-fetching games (311,444
lifetimes) with keys previous depth, team units and building type,
predicts how far a worker should settle a scheduled walking field. Its
committed default is p80, chosen by measured timing of the scheduled
pipeline (docs/building-gradient-depth-model.md). The depth only moves CPU
between threads, never results. test/test_gradient_depth_fit.py checks
that regenerating the header is a no-op and that the C++ lookup agrees
with the fitter.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Schedule building walking field refreshes on workers

A stale building walking field (dirty, topology generation, clearing timer
or a stuck unit) is no longer rebuilt on the simulation thread. Team
stepping requests a refresh and keeps serving the old field. After the
tick up to four requests are staged; the observation boundary captures
their owner scalars and immutable cost planes in O(1) with the periodic
job's snapshot, and one executor batch seeds and searches them on workers
(SeedCells buildingCells, BuildingGradientSearch::Inputs and
resolveToCost). BuildingGradientPipeline publishes each result
buildingGradientDelay ticks after capture, before team stepping, by
swapping the field and its search; a partial field resumes from its own
buckets. A synchronous rebuild, a reset or a reused destination
supersedes a pending result. Access metadata (locked) follows the newest
capture. Team-wide resets and forbidden-area paints keep stale walking
fields serving and refresh them on schedule.

Synchronous builds remain where the design needs them: fields a building
has never had or lost to idle eviction or its own move, type or range
change, queue overflow beyond 64 requests, and maps without a game.
The generated depth model sets how far a worker settles each field;
readers still resolve unsettled cells, so the depth never changes a
result. GLOB2_BUILDING_DEPTH=full|table|lazy overrides it for timing,
and with gradient statistics on, scheduled publications end lifetimes as
rebuilds do and default to lazy depth so rows record readers' needs.

buildingGradientDelay is a match rule (1-8, default 8) in GameHeader,
the rule parser, MatchSetup in C++ and TypeScript and the protocol
fixtures; it cannot change with pending fields. --fork-rule
buildingGradientDelay=N forks a loaded game without pending fields to
another delay; the fork, and every save, applies the header's delay to an
empty pipeline first, and an empty saved section of another delay loads.
Format 148 saves the delay, the request queue and
completed pending fields (searches finished first, so no queues are
serialized); older saves restore no pending work. result.json gains
building_gradient_* counters.

Greedy-only fetching and scheduled building walking fields change what

commits.subject: Animate water as travelling waves across a 4x4-cell block (#945)
commits.body:
* Animate water as travelling waves across a 4x4-cell block

Water and deep water were sixteen unrelated random variants stepping
through four phases in lockstep, so open sea read as a grid of 32 px
squares. They are now cells of one periodic 4x4-cell block, chosen by
position through a new render-only catalog key, "variant_grid". The
synthesiser renders a sum of plane waves with whole wave numbers on that
block, each advancing whole cycles over a sixteen-phase loop (6 ticks per
phase, the same 96-tick loop as before). Every cell animates locally on
the shared clock and the field continues across all cell edges, so swell
crests roll toward the lower right with cross chop breaking them into
glints. Deep water reads the same field, so crests carry on across the
shallow/deep blend.

Faster phases recompose terrain pages more often, and mixed shore cells
dominated that cost by re-sampling coverage. Pages now keep each mixed
cell's coverage next to an animated material (bounded to a quarter of the
page budget) and only re-blend textures on a phase change. Composition
goes through the same mask path whether kept or not, so pixels are
unchanged.

commits.subject: Predict scheduled building field depth from the field's own past depths (#957)
commits.body:
* Give each gradient_depth map size its own generator pool

A gradient_depth size entry may now carry a `generators` list, so a campaign

and colony count, instead of only those that generate at every size. Sizes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Predict scheduled building field depth from the field's own past depths

A scheduled building walking field is settled on a worker to a predicted
depth, and readers settle anything deeper lazily on the owner. The depth now
comes from the field's own history, read when its refresh is staged: with m the
deeper of the serving field's settled depth so far and the replaced
lifetime's final depth (settledCostHint),

    depth = offset + (slope256 * m) >> 8

with two integers per operating point. A field with neither depth (after a
save is loaded) settles only its seeds. The quantile table over previous depth,
team units and building type is gone, and the model no longer names building
types, so new buildings need no refit.

Fit 3: 1,472 gradient_depth games, 3.41M scheduled footprint lifetimes. Held
out by game, the default (lambda 0.5) moves 0.902 of the owner's lazy search to
workers at 1.17x search CPU. Fit 2's table, as the engine runs it, moved 0.781 at
1.22x: it keyed on the previous lifetime's final depth, which the engine never
has at staging. Each point maximises owner saving minus lambda times extra search
CPU; a 48x48 table over both depths, and richer formulas, scored the same, and
building type, level, construction state, team size, workers or game time added
at most 0.0005.

tools/gradient_depth_fit.py now needs numpy: datasets are column arrays
(.npz), work curves are built by bincount over (fold, group, label) cells, and
the integer search scores every candidate for all lambdas in one pass. On fit 3
it builds the dataset in under a minute and fits in about ten seconds, with the
same constants the pure-Python search found. Regenerating the header from the
committed summary still needs only the standard library.

Building field statistics record the inputs as they stood at staging
(staged, previous_hint, serving_settled), which is what the engine reads.
GLOB2_BUILDING_DEPTH also accepts an operating point name for timing. The depth
never changes results: per-tick checksums match across every point, full and
lazy, so no SIM_REVISION, save or replay change is involved.

commits.subject: Build Lava shield from catalogue lava, fords and volcanic ground (#973)
commits.body:
* Build Lava shield from catalogue lava, fords and volcanic ground

Revision 5 of the Lava shield generator uses the terrain catalogue. The
tongues are lava with an ember fringe, impassable on foot and avoided by
fliers; each tongue that reaches the sea keeps one scree ford. The crater
is a lava lake with void vents, ash inside the rim circuit and loam and
moss outside it. Side branches are cooled scree and gravel. Roads are dirt
tracks and the far sea is deep water.

Stone becomes a crust along the flows. The crust, scree aprons and ash
are laid after the towns, rings and roads are fixed, so they never take a
town's room, and towns may sit on rim loam, which they turn back to grass.
Flows swell and spread into toes, and corner strokes are half a tile
thinner so the walls cover the tiles the old stone tongues did.

Validation now checks the lava walls and that every ford is open ground
the colonies reach, in place of the structural stone. The golden rows and
the online pool pin move to revision 5.
